📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Samsung has officially released the One UI 9.5 beta for Galaxy S26 people.

Recent findings suggest that after weeks of testing and rumors, Samsung has officially announced the One UI 9.5 beta for Galaxy S26 customers. According to the company's announcement, the beta will give users an early look at One UI 9.5 ahead of its stable release. We expect the stable version of One UI 9.5 to arrive alongside the Galaxy S27 series launch next year, but until then, the beta will give users a taste of what's coming.

As for what's newly introduced, Samsung says One UI 9.5 introduces updated camera controls that give people more flexibility and creative control when taking photos and videos. According to the manufacturer, enhanced Pro and Pro Video modes offer customizable controls and presets for different shooting conditions.

There's also a newly introduced Mindful Note feature that allows customers to express their feelings and journal their thoughts, similar to what's already available through Apple's Journal app and Google's Pixel Journal.

Alongside this, Samsung is introducing a newly introduced medication tracking feature that allows users to add prescriptions, vitamins, and supplements, set customized reminders, and keep track of their medications directly from their phones.

In a recent development, probably the best feature Samsung has introduced with One UI 9.5 is the ability to lock individual apps. Until now, owners had to rely on Secure Folder to keep apps behind biometric authentication. But Samsung is finally giving users more flexibility with App Lock.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

The company says consumers will be able to keep individual apps private by locking them behind biometric authentication or their screen lock. Samsung also says that when an app is locked, its notification content and widgets will be hidden as well.

It has been revealed that in addition to this, One UI 9.5 introduces a dedicated floating shortcut button that gives users quick access to frequently used controls. There are also improved hearing aid controls, allowing users to adjust the volume directly from the notification panel.

For now, Samsung has started rolling out the One UI 9.5 beta to Galaxy S26 users in select countries. You'll need to enroll through the Samsung Members app to try it out. However, if you'd rather wait for the stable enhancement, you'll likely have to wait another couple of months until the Galaxy S27 series debuts next year.

In a recent development, tipster Ice Universe has also shared the One UI 9.5 changelog on X. Here's everything latest in the first build of One UI 9.5:.

- A cleaner interface makes camera settings easier to access and compare without excessive scrolling. The bottom control area has been redesigned for more convenient operation.

1.2 Enhanced Pro Mode and Pro Video.

- Improved shutter speed and frame rate controls.

- More precise shutter speed adjustments.

- A redesigned audio control interface in Pro Video mode.

2.1 Live Effects for the Lock Screen.

- Add dynamic depth effects to your lock screen.

- Elements in the wallpaper move at different speeds when the device is tilted, creating a sense of depth.

- Choose from 10-second, 30-second, 1-minute, 5-minute, and 10-minute time intervals.

- Customize these settings through the clock options in the upper-right corner of the lock screen editor.

2.3 Expanded Now Bar Animations.

More Now Bar animations are available across different scenarios.

- Enjoy dynamic visual effects for supported sports events, including team scores and victories.

- Set a waiting period of up to 10 seconds before selected apps open.

- Designed to reduce impulsive app usage and encourage more mindful screen time.

- Protect individual apps using a PIN, pattern, password, or biometric authentication.

- Keep sensitive app content secure when sharing your device.

4.2 Enhanced Privacy Display (Supported Models).

- Privacy Display can activate automatically when entering a PIN, pattern, or password.

- Additional support for private Gallery albums and locked Samsung Notes.

- Automatic activation options for selected apps and notifications.

4.3 Improved Biometric Authentication.

- Enhanced facial recognition and fingerprint authentication.

- Support for authentication flows involving both biometric methods.

- Fingerprint authentication can be completed directly on the sensor without an additional on-screen confirmation.

4.4 Redesigned Biometric Enrollment.

- Fingerprint and facial recognition setup screens feature a cleaner interface and refined animations.

5.1 Built-in Office Document Preview.

- Preview DOCX and PPTX files directly in My Files without installing Microsoft Office.

- PPTX slideshow playback is also supported.

5.2 Improved Storage Management.

- Easier selection and deletion of uncategorized files and files right now in use when managing storage.

6.1 Improved Maximized Window Experience.

- Maximized windows can occupy more screen space.

- Refined status bar and taskbar layouts provide a more immersive desktop experience.

- More window snapping options beyond traditional split-screen layouts.

- Arrange two, three, or four applications on the screen simultaneously.

7.1 Sleep Coaching Improvements.

#2074. Latest Update: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (925 w)

AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Banks Have Had It Up to Here With Your AI Agent

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (925 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Wells Fargo is set to enact an updated agreement with millions of customers, specifically about AI agents, starting on Tuesday.
  • Recent findings suggest that AI agents, which automate online tasks and click on your behalf, have stumbled through 2026.
  • Builders of these AI tools often market agents as the ultimate tool for shopping decisions, whether that’s putting together a grocery order, finding accommodations for a vacation, or discovering specific holiday gifts for your parents.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Wells Fargo is set to enact an updated agreement with millions of customers, specifically about AI agents, starting on Tuesday. The bank’s warning to early adopters could not be clearer. “Your use of any AI Agent is AT YOUR OWN RISK,” read Wells Fargo’s new terms.

Recent findings suggest that AI agents, which automate online tasks and click on your behalf, have stumbled through 2026. They remain nascent technology, but a growing subset of power people latched onto the personal bots this year. Sometimes these early adopters enjoyed the efficient help of automation, and other times they publicly embarrassed themselves when the AI agents made major mistakes, like posting bank details for everyone at work to see.

Builders of these AI tools often market agents as the ultimate tool for shopping decisions, whether that’s putting together a grocery order, finding accommodations for a vacation, or discovering specific holiday gifts for your parents. I’ve used an agent to help shop for a latest couch, comparing options within a specific budget and tracking price drops.

Industry observers note that some consumers value these agents so much that they are oblivious to the overarching security concerns, pairing account credentials and granting permissions for the agents to take sweeping actions without forethought. Although the segment of online transactions completed by these autonomous tools remains minuscule, US-based banking institutions are already sick of third-party AI agents.

It’s not just banks; AI agents are igniting turf wars around the web. Amazon, one of the largest online retailers, blocked Meta’s Muse, one of the most widely used AI agents, from making purchases on its platform. Travel companies are also pushing back—United recently unveiled that personal bots would be blocked from purchasing flights on your behalf.

The automation, which remains a central selling point of always-on agents, is exactly what may get users in trouble. “Consumers authorize goals, not every click,” indicates Kacy Kim, an associate professor of marketing at Bryant University who studies consumer behavior and emerging tech. While Kim expects some consumers to feel like it's unfair to be held accountable for their agent’s mistakes, she doesn’t expect these policy moves by financial institutions to scare off the early-adopter crowd already in deep and using the tools as part of everyday life.

In a recent development, banks appear to be trying to get ahead of major issues, in case agentic tools stick around and don’t just disappear as another tech fad. “All of our data highlights that most people don't even know what agents are, much less use them,” states Sucharita Kodali, a Forrester analyst who focuses on ecommerce and consumer behavior. She sees banks as fundamentally risk-averse, so taking proactive measures now makes sense, even if most agentic issues remain edge cases.

“The banks see risks with everything,” she says. “From the security of transactions to automated withdrawals that could happen to the detriment of account holders.”.

Sources indicate that even though outliers exist, many users are aware of the risks and are only comfortable handing over so much control to an AI agent, and only for certain shopping tasks. “People are very comfortable with AI buying toilet paper,” says Luca Cian, a professor at the University of Virginia who studies consumer psychology and AI.

It has been revealed that he sees consumers as increasingly comfortable turning to AI tools for shopping advice but often only automating boring buys, like household supplies. Shoppers are less comfortable automating away dynamic, big-ticket purchases that require additional care and discretion.

In a recent development, cian gives a hypothetical scenario where a customer’s AI agent accidentally buys 10 roasted chickens from the supermarket. Who’s to blame? The retailer would likely argue that they completed a valid order that you placed. The AI builder may claim that they just provided the software, and even included disclaimers about potential mistakes. And now your bank is making it clear they don’t want to be held responsible either. Hope you need the protein, because it looks like you just bought 10 hot chickens.

Certain credit cards, though, are looking into limited protections for shoppers. Mainly, American Express announced that some agentic mistakes, like ordering too many of a certain item, may be eligible for reimbursement in the future through the card provider if you can't get your money back from the original retailer.

Sources indicate that banks are pumping out reasonable warnings about third-party agents, but don’t get it twisted. These banks are all-in on first-party tools. “Banks are doing two things at once,” Cian indicates. “They're locking the door to outside agents and building their own.” Customers have interacted with Wells Fargo’s tool that answers questions using generative AI over a billion times. Bank of America revamped its upcoming EricaAssist agent this year to help employees. Citigroup even rolled out an internal development platform specifically centered on agents.

Despite all the hype, Kodali remains skeptical about whether all of this hoopla is even necessary. “The issue with agents and shopping is that, first of all, it is not difficult to buy on Amazon or Walmart or anywhere else,” she states. “In most of those transactions, you don't need an agent.” Agentic shopping often seems to be a solution in search of a problem. Or at least an attempt by AI builders to find a way to earn affiliate revenue, eventually, from their software tools.

Whether AI agents grow in popularity for shopping automation or slowly fade into the digital graveyard, banks are already resolute on the matter. It’s your bot, and your problem.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The creator economy has exploded in recent years. TV indicates feature creators doing cameos as themselves, your favorite author is probably on BookTok, and Starbucks is paying baristas to make creator-style videos.

In a survey from The Conversation, more than 60 percent of middle and high school students remarked they wanted to be influencers or have a career based on what they saw online.

Industry observers note that at Mashable, we’re constantly covering what’s happening in the creator world, whether that’s at VidCon, the TikTok Awards, or in conversations across the internet. For our "Creator Playbook" series, we ask creators how they turn content into a career and about the tools they use to do so for "In My Bag.".

Industry observers note that in our inaugural Creators’ Choice Awards, we surveyed our favorite creators across the internet, including some of our Mashable 101 nominees. We wanted to know which gear and tools they use to see which brands and products are the most loved among digital creators. Now, we're ready to announce the winners.

According to recent reports, A smartphone is the most basic tool a creator holds in their toolkit. Not only does it act as the camera, microphone, editor, and uploader, but it's also how they connect with followers.

In our own reporting, Senior Reporter Haley Henschel wrote, "For most of us, our phone is the most important device we own," calling it a "lifeline to friends" and "our primary gateway to the internet." She also noted that unless you carry around a separate camera, your phone is also how you document the world.

Phones are where people create and consume content. So, of course, we wanted to ask creators which phone brands they use and love.

In a recent development, no surprise, our pool of creators overwhelmingly use Apple iPhones. They cited that they prefer Apple because the phones are easy to use and do everything they need from a mobile device. Most of our respondents had an iPhone 15 or newer.

“My entire life, business, and career [are] managed and created using my iPhone,” one respondent wrote.

Mashable's resident iPhone reviewer, Senior Editor Stan Schroeder, called all of the latest iPhones "blazing fast," and has lauded their cameras, battery life, and impressively fast performance in his reviews.

It has been revealed that some creators also commented on the phones’ long battery lives and impressive performance and features. One person said, “This phone is a workhorse,” while another called their iPhone “a power performer” that “gets everything you need done with a snap, with excellent battery life and storage.”.

We know that Apple loyalty runs deep, so we suspected it would hold the top spot among our surveyed creators. One even called themself “a forever customer of the brand.”.

Sources indicate that samsung Galaxy phones were a second favorite among our creator pool. Samsung stood out for its cameras and overall satisfaction with its phones. Per our reporting, Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra is "faster than some mid-range laptops we've tried," and the brand makes the best foldable Android phone.

“It is the best phone available,” remarked one respondent who has a Samsung Galaxy S26+. Another creator agreed that “Samsung makes the best phones, period.”.

Survey respondents praised Samsung’s operating system, processor, AI integration, and long battery life.

“I do the majority of my content creation on my phone and find it very easy to use,” one creator stated.

Industry observers note that while a phone might be the most accessible or most-used tool for content creation, some creators take video editing or design work to their personal computers. Henschel writes, "The best laptops are fast enough for their primary use cases, well-made, and priced fairly for their specs." We were curious which machines power our favorite creators’ content, and the results were pretty split among different brands.

Though, our creators did choose laptop brands that Mashable experts personally recommend.

Sources indicate that apple reigned supreme as the most preferred laptop brand for our survey takers. They like MacBooks for their compatibility with other Apple devices, sleek design, and overall usability.

"It looks nice and it works for so many things," one respondent wrote. "There is nothing you can't do on it — it's definitely worth the price.".

Creators also reported that the software they use to create their content runs well on Apple laptops and that the MacBooks are fast.

One creator wrote, “As a musician, I love the MacBook Pro because of its capabilities for creating music and music content. I frequently run Logic Pro and MuseScore on my MacBook to create music, both of which run super smoothly. I also use it to edit videos featuring my music for social media. I would definitely recommend this computer to another musician.”.

Another said their MacBook is “very capable” of doing what they need when putting together content.

Industry observers note that apple’s laptops are definitely a favorite for creatives. “It's great for everything you need as a content creator,” wrote one respondent.

Sources indicate that our creators also prefer Dell for their computing needs. Multiple people noted the longevity of their Dell laptops, with one noting that they’ve had theirs for more than 10 years.

Respondents noted simply, “I love my Dell,” and “It’s my favorite.”.

Sources indicate that other comments praised Dell’s processing speed, RAM capacity, battery life, ease of use, and durability. These same qualities are why you'll find multiple Dell computers on our list of the best Windows laptops.

Participants in our Creators’ Choice survey also preferred Microsoft laptops. They lauded the laptops' speed, processor, and design, with one person commenting specifically on how easy it is for them to create and edit vlogs.

One creator put it simply: “It's an all-rounder and is good for most people.”.

The final winner in the laptop category is HP. Creators love the brand’s laptops for their speed, quality, and affordability.

“My HP laptop is fast, reliable, and handles everyday tasks with ease,” wrote one participant, adding that it’s actually a great value for its price.

Others noted HP’s ease in multitasking and the power behind its laptops. One creator stated, “It is easy to use, affordable, durable, and can be used for many things such as recording, video calls, and editing pictures.”.

While video is arguably the most popular medium for creators in 2026, many still use photo-editing tools and incorporate photography into their feeds.

It has been revealed that adobe reigns supreme in editing tools for our creators, including its photo-centric tools like Photoshop and Lightroom. Many respondents praised Adobe apps’ ease of use and their editing tools for both professionals and hobbyists.

Multiple people said Adobe is their “go-to” editing tool and that it’s “the best I’ve ever used.”.

Recent findings suggest that “This photo editing software is amazing, and I swear by it,” wrote a survey respondent. “The results speak for themselves.”.

One person mentioned that Adobe’s AI features “make editing so much more efficient” and that they’d recommend it based on that alone.

Industry observers note that the second-most preferred photo editing tool among our survey pool is Canva. Creators love that it’s accessible and easy to use, even for non-professionals.

One comment said, “I like that it's free to use and still has good editing tools for free consumers.”.

Videos make up the majority of creator-made content on social media, whether on TikTok, Instagram Reels, or YouTube, and our creators have two favorite video editing brands.

Sources indicate that adobe was their top choice again, with a large number of responses noting how easy the programs are to use. One creator called Adobe Premiere “an amazing software,” while another said it’s “perfect for what I need it for.”.

Others commented on Adobe being a great editing platform and having a good variety of editing tools.

Another favorite video editing tool among our creator pool is CapCut. The mobile-first editing program is incredibly easy to use, according to our respondents. They also like it for its TikTok integration.

One respondent who states they’ve been an avid CapCut user before it was even called CapCut wrote, “It’s been the best editing software I’ve ever used.”.

Affordability is another area where CapCut shines — one creator called it “a steal.”.

Graphic design can enhance your content with stronger visuals or allow you to create recognizable branding.

And, once again, Adobe was a favorite for our creators. They prefer it for its ease of use and breadth of tools.

One creator said Adobe has a “great comprehensive suite of design and editing tools that are crucial to making the best content.”.

Another called Adobe the “best in the business.”.

Canva was another top choice in our survey results. People prefer it because it’s also very easy to use and free or affordable.

“I like Canva because it has great tools that make editing more fun,” wrote one respondent.

Another said, “It can do lots of different things to make great products.”.

Though smartphones have pretty stellar onboard cameras, many creators still opt for a dedicated vlogging camera. You'll find an array of cameras featured in our In My Bag series, but these are the top three brands, according to the creators who took our survey.

Canon was the favorite camera brand among the survey pool. They praised Canon cameras’ great quality and durability. One person remarked their Canon PowerShot G7 X “has been a great camera that lasted through the years.”.

Recent findings suggest that creators from our survey also use and like Sony vlogging cameras. They recommend Sony cameras for beginners and pros alike. One respondent said, “I recommend them because they have very good quality; they are certainly very good investments.”.

Creators also like Panasonic for its audio quality, image quality, battery life, and user-friendliness.

While we had creators answering questions about their favorite tools and gear, we, of course, also had to ask them about which social media platform they use the most. Drumroll please….

Facebook actually came out on top as the most-used social media among our respondents.

They like Facebook mostly for personal use and keeping up with friends and family members. Many people mentioned the platform is great for connecting with others.

“I have been using it for years and is the best way i have found to stay in touch with people and share my story,” said one respondent.

According to recent reports, on the subject of using Facebook for years, one person called it “the O.G. of social media,” adding that “there is nothing not to like” about it.

Industry observers note that another Meta platform was also a favorite: Creators like Instagram for how easy it is to use and for connecting with friends and followers. According to one creator, “it offers a visually engaging platform to connect with friends, family, and global communities.”.

Others praised the creativity and engagement of the platform, shouting out its wide array of content types.

One of the creators said, “I love using Instagram,” calling it “one of the best social platforms around.”.

The next most-used social media platform is TikTok. Many of the creators we talk to and write about use TikTok as their main platform. Our survey group likes TikTok for its large audience, universal appeal, and fun content.

It has been revealed that according to one respondent, it’s the best place to get a start on social media. Once you’ve gotten that start, one creator noted, “It's a good platform for people who want to share their life or creations through short-form videos. Or if they want to post short clips from their longer videos to attract viewers to their YouTube channel.”.

It has been revealed that and that brings us to our creator pool's final favorite social media platform: YouTube. Similar to TikTok, one creator said, “It's a great place to post your content, whether long or short form, and is used by millions.”.

Others love it for the easy-to-use platform and quality features, calling it “fun and cool” and “better than the other brands.”.

Sources indicate that apple today announced that App Store prices for apps and In-App Purchases will be adjusted in five countries starting December 3, following changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates. Here are the details.

In a new post published on its developer portal, Apple today confirmed a series of changes to App Store pricing, as well as updates to tax rules affecting developers and customers in several countries, including the US.

According to the company, developers’ proceeds from eligible app and In-App Purchase sales have been adjusted in four countries, reflecting the following tax updates:.

Specific to Botswana and Rwanda, Apple said that “Exhibit B of the Paid Applications Agreement will be updated to indicate that Apple collects and remits applicable taxes.”.

Recent findings suggest that apple added that a latest “Software as a Service (SaaS)” attribute is now available for several App Store tax categories, including App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting. Developers can review and revision their tax category selections in App Store Connect.

Additionally, starting December 3, developers who rely on Apple’s automatic pricing adjustments will see changes to app and In-App Purchase prices in:.

Apple usually makes these adjustments to account for changes in taxes and foreign exchange rates, and notes that prices won’t change in countries selected as the base storefront, for auto-renewable subscriptions, or in storefronts where developers manually manage their prices.

The announcement does not go into detail about how much prices will change in each country, or whether they will increase or decrease.

Finally, starting January 1, 2027, apps and In-App Purchases in the SaaS, App Store Software, Software Training Material, Dating, and Boosting categories will become subject to sales and use taxes in California.

Apple noted that “prices on the United States storefront are displayed to customers exclusive of taxes, so the tax change will not affect them,” but added that while developers’ proceeds will remain unchanged, “the total amount customers are charged, inclusive of tax, may increase.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rumors are back about an old theory about Samsung's current-gen phones. Some claim the organization is seriously considering bringing back an older aperture feature for future cameras.

These rumors resurfaced after tipster Yogesh Brar suggested a classic return could grace Samsung's next Galaxy S phones in a couple of years. Brar claims Samsung is considering bringing variable aperture back to its Galaxy S flagship phones (via GSMArena). However, if true, consumers shouldn't expect this on every phone.

Recent findings suggest that brar says Samsung might explore this only with the Galaxy S28 Pro and S28 Ultra. If this is anything to go by, perhaps we should expect the Pro to stick around. Recent rumors suggest the alleged Galaxy S27 Pro will feel like an Ultra, but be positioned between it and the Plus (despite its supposed specs).

The tipster also suggests that Samsung "isn't the only brand exploring VA for their flagship device.".

Would Samsung only bring this back for the sake of competition?

Recent findings suggest that we're going to walk back through history. In late 2025, rumors surfaced that Samsung was considering bringing back variable aperture on its Galaxy S phones. These rumors claimed the Korean OEM was doing so to better contend with Apple's upcoming 2025 iPhones: the iPhone 18 and 18 Pro Max. Samsung hasn't had variable aperture since the Galaxy S9 days. It was a feature that covered narrow and wide apertures to help users take photos in a range of situations.

Several months later, rumors remarked variable aperture was headed to the Galaxy S26 series (which didn't happen). However, reports said Samsung was working with its Electro-Mechanics and MCNEX teams on the required tech. This would've enabled "true" variable aperture, letting the camera lens easily shift between apertures. It wouldn't have been digital, like the Galaxy S25 Ultra.

It has been revealed that if we can expect this in two years, how limited would it be? Remember: the Galaxy S9 and even the S10 had variable aperture, but it was restricted to shifting between f/1.5 and f/2.4. Truthfully, that's not good enough for above-average output.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Apple this week revealed the additional Siri AI usage you’ll get if you have an iCloud+ subscription. This ranges from doubled limits for a 200GB initiative to 20 times for a 12TB plan.

However, the organization’s support document reveals that some countries will not get access to these increased usage allowances ….

It has been revealed that apple hasn’t yet specified the standard limits applicable to Siri AI usage, instead saying that these will vary depending on anything from the feature used to the overall level of demand at the time. However, it did list the proportional increases you get with paid iCloud aims.

However, tucked away in the small print in the company’s support document are some exclusions. One of them is no surprise: EU countries.

Siri AI isn’t available at all in the EU due to Apple’s perception of potential antitrust problems. Essentially, Apple believes that if it introduces Siri AI there, it will be required to give competing AI services the same level of access to its devices. But three other countries are specifically excluded:.

Apple gives no explanation, simply saying:.

Increased access to Siri AI with iCloud+ is subject to Siri AI availability and is not available in Brazil, the EU, UK, or South Korea.

However, I have a strong suspicion about the reason.

What all three countries have in common is that they’ve taken a strong antitrust stance with Apple on a number of occasions over a range of complications.

Recent findings suggest that it may be that Apple has genuine concerns about how regulators might respond if they effectively throw in free access to increased Siri AI usage. The company may fear that this would be viewed as anti-competitive by implicitly disadvantaging other AI services.

Sources indicate that A less charitable take would be that Apple is firing a warning shot across the bows of these countries, seeking to communicate that there are consequences for what it views as attacks on its ecosystem. If customers are angered by missing out, Apple might be hoping that these feelings would be directed at regulators rather than the iPhone maker.

What’s your take? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google is giving millions of people access to Gemini's Tasks feature for free.

The tool can run multi-step requests in the background, and Google is expanding its capabilities to include shopping, phone calls, email, and deeper integrations into its apps.

Formerly known as Spark, Tasks is now rolling out to free Gemini consumers in the US, Japan, South Korea, Canada, Australia, and India, as per Josh Woodward, VP of Product for AI at Google. This agentic mode previously required a paid AI Pro or AI Ultra tier.

In a recent development, gemini can now do your tasks free of charge in six countries! We’ve built it for anyone who has tasks piling up during all the classes, meetings, and school drop-offs that fill the day. Our goal is for Gemini to get the job done and save you time and money along the way. 3 major updates: 1) Running on our new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, Gemini can get stuff done at no cost for hundreds of millions of people across the US, Japan, Korea, Canada, Australia, and India. 2) Many highly requested features are rolling out now, starting in the US: * Call local businesses (via Google Duplex) * Pay and check out (via Google Pay) * Text Gemini on Android or iOS (via RCS) * Forward emails to Gemini (via Gmail) * Sign into sites without sharing passwords outside Google (via Google Password Manager) 3) We’ve also landed our biggest update yet for the Gemini <> Google Workspace integration. The tools trigger more reliably, and you can do much more without ever leaving Gemini. Draft or send emails. Create and edit Docs or Sheets. Add multiple Calendar events at once. Ready to hand off your next task? We can’t wait to see what Gemini crosses off your list first.November 17, 2026.

It runs on Google’s new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model and allows people to switch from Chat to Task mode to pass off work instead of babysitting every step. That could involve asking Gemini to initiative a trip, research a topic, set up a morning briefing, or manage recurring tasks while you’re busy doing literally anything else.

To test it, flip the toggle above your mobile prompt box (or below on the web) from "Chat" to "Task." You can even bypass the app entirely by forwarding emails or texting Gemini directly through Google Messages and iMessage.

The Workspace integration is also receiving a major upgrade. Google claims Gemini can now more reliably draft or send emails, create and edit Google Docs and Sheets, and add multiple events to Google Calendar without toggling between apps.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

As you can imagine, having an AI in your inbox, passwords, and payment methods does raise some security concerns. Google says when browsing the web, Tasks runs inside an isolated virtual machine, protected against prompt injection and Google Safe Browsing protections. Gemini also asks for confirmation before it buys anything and can ask for clarification if your instructions aren’t clear.

Sources indicate that that said, Google still has some work to do. Some sites might prevent Gemini from completing a task and ask you to step in and finish the last step. For now, the promise of a digital assistant that can really take work off your hands is getting closer — but still isn’t quite ready to be trusted with everything.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A set of major tech outages in close succession is leading some to speculate that they are connected, and that the US is under systemic attack by a hostile state.

All the evidence suggests otherwise, with individual explanations for each of them – and the White House is now saying as much in a bid to put fears to rest ….

Whether there was or wasn't a cyber attack, I wouldn't believe a single word from the White House.

On Thursday, a widespread Microsoft 365 outage ran into the following day when two unrelated issues coincided. Friday saw a nationwide ground stop of US air traffic due to a communication issue affecting all air traffic control centers. On Monday, a bug in a Chase bank system saw disruption not only to the bank itself, but also other banks where Chase was a party to a transaction. Finally, yesterday saw many Apple services offline, with retail stores also affected.

The Apple outage doesn’t appear to have been significant enough to have reached the administration’s radar, but CBS News reports secretary of state Marco Rubio saying the others are unrelated.

Sources indicate that “The Microsoft incident has nothing to do with what we saw with the FAA. The FAA has nothing to do with what we saw with the banks a few days ago. These issues that we’ve seen from a technical standpoint are completely unrelated one from another,” Rubio said […].

Sources indicate that “We have zero evidence or any reason to believe that any of these isolated or individual instances have anything to do with nefarious actors, with cyber hackers, with criminals, with another nation state, with a malign actor of any kind. Each of them are distinct, and they’re different in their causation.”.

The statement was backed by Senator Mark Warner.

In a recent development, democratic Sen. Mark Warner, vice chair of the Senate Intelligence Committee, also noted on Tuesday that there’s no indication these incidents are the result of an attack.

Warner went on to say that the ability of AI systems to find vulnerabilities at “unprecedented speed” does, however, mean companies and government agencies alike need to be ready to patch vulnerabilities immediately.

Best Gifts for Mom (2026): Digital Wall Calendars, Better Bags, Personalized Jewelry, and More

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Moms give the best gifts, so it stands to reason that you should get the best gifts for Mom when you're shopping for her in any scenario.
  • Recent findings suggest that if you're worried you're going to give her a disappointing gift or something she already has, fear not: I've gathered the coolest things we recommend here at WIRED that just about any mom will love.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Moms give the best gifts, so it stands to reason that you should get the best gifts for Mom when you're shopping for her in any scenario. That includes Mother's Day, her birthday, Christmas, Hanukkah, or any other holiday in your family's life that includes gift-giving. The holiday season is now upon us, and I've added a few gift ideas with that time of year in mind.

Recent findings suggest that if you're worried you're going to give her a disappointing gift or something she already has, fear not: I've gathered the coolest things we recommend here at WIRED that just about any mom will love. From wellness gadgets that can improve her skin to the best tote bags I've tried, and even a device that puts her digital calendar in an IRL device, moms everywhere can get a ton out of these gifts. Many of these are items I've given to my mother, or other WIRED staffers have given to theirs. Or they might be at the top of my own wish list as a mother of a 4-year-old.

Updated November 2026: I've added Therabody's Theraface Mask Glo, Omnilux's Contour Gloves, WanderFull's HydroBag, and Nuuly's clothing subscription as new gifts to this guide.

The must-have gadget for women of almost any age is an LED mask. These masks promise to use red light to erase wrinkles, brighten your skin, and keep acne at bay. I haven't seen much change in my wrinkles in my year-plus of regularly using a red-light mask, but I can confirm it makes my skin brighter and calms down acne and scars much faster when I'm regularly treating my skin, and I always get compliments on how nice my skin looks when I'm regularly using it. Therabody's TheraFace Mask Glo has a range of treatments with both red and blue light, a unique vibration therapy feature, and removable eye shields if you don't want the light in your eyes.

Look, nothing claims mom life like looking for the perfect bag. I'm in a massive tote phase of my life; I somehow need to either lug an armload of items for myself and my son (or just myself!) or I only need a tiny belt bag. There's no in between.

In a recent development, the Yardsale Day Bag has been my go-to for a variety of needs, from a colorful personal item for a flight to a gym bag to the aerial studio. It's got a waterproof bottom that makes me happy to bring it to the zoo's splash pad, and a magnetic middle separator you can flex to separate the middle of the bag into two medium sections to better divide all your items. Plus, there are a handful of side pockets inside, but none are large enough for my massive Owala water bottle. I have the 30L in Butter, but there's also a smaller 20L version if you're looking for something a little more compact.

Industry observers note that if your mom wants something a little more stylish, the Alex Mill totes are always on my mind. They come in a variety of gorgeous colors and are made of coated canvas, so they can put up with daily adventures, and you can customize them with your mom's initials (or even just the word “mom”!) with Alex Mill's hand-painted letter service. It's a simpler tote with no other pockets, but you can use the top snaps to let out the sides or tuck them in, depending on how much space Mom needs on a given day. The weathered color and vibe of these bags also feel perfect for the fall season.

Sources indicate that my latest favorite family planning gadget is a digital wall calendar. These handy devices take the Google Calendar I live by (and just about any other digital calendar, if your mom isn't a Google girl) and put it on a physical device I can quickly tap into without needing to grab my phone or bark at Alexa. The Skylight Calendar 2 is my favorite, because it not only includes to-do lists, meal planning, and a recipe book but also doubles as a digital photo frame. That means it displays cute photos of my family most of the time, and then, with a simple tap, it opens the calendar or whatever page I was last on to show me what's on my family's schedule. It does have a subscription fee, though, to get the digital photo frame feature and a few other options, like meal planning. But I think it's well worth it to get so many features in a single device. You can also gift her kiddo a Skylight Buddy ($140) so that she doesn't have to remind them to check the main calendar for their chores; it'll appear on their own device if they have a Buddy.

To me, motherhood is all about change. It's most obvious at the start of motherhood, when your body changes a lot over the course of nine months, but motherhood encompasses the rest of our lives, and our bodies and style change a lot over that time. One of the biggest giveaways that time has gone by is our clothes—how well they fit for our current stage, whether they reflect the time of our life right now, and if we're bored out of our skull with everything but don't want to buy an entirely fresh closet.

I've been loving renting from Nuuly this pregnancy because the brand has an entire maternity section that lets me find pieces to fit me in this short—but very different size—season of my life. My older mother also loves having a clothing subscription because she gets bored of her outfit options to wear into the office, and I loved it for the same reason when I had my first clothing subscription right out of college. If Mom has been talking about wanting some newly introduced looks but feels overwhelmed about what she wants to invest in, these rental services are a fun way to get a lot of new clothes in your life without having to store them or spend as much as you would have (some of my favorite maternity clothes I've gotten through Nuuly would have cost me $200 apiece!) The service costs $98 a month, but your first month is discounted to just $60. There's one piece I miss already that might drive me to pick up a second subscription, which would genuinely be cheaper than buying the piece I want brand new.

For years, the go-to gift for a woman in my family, mother or not, was shopping in the jewelry section of a department store. My mom even helped orchestrate this for the rest of the aunties and grandmas, but now, as a mom myself, I find myself interested in jewelry that tells a story about my family and children instead of just any old set. (Except extra earrings for my earring stack, a gift I'm thrilled to get, because there's never enough.).

I love these pieces from Gorjana and BaubleBar that you can customize. Gorjana has a ton of charms you can add to its necklaces or bracelets to reflect Mom’s kids’ initials, birthstones, or anything else; I paired a charm of my son’s first initial ($50) with the Wilshire Adjustable Necklace ($68). If she's more of a ring gal, BaubleBar's Toi et Moi ring ($78) lets you choose two birthstones to display. I chose my and my son's birthstones, but luckily his sibling-to-be will also have a red birthstone, so it'll remain a perfect reflection of my kids and me for years to come.

Sources indicate that this item was literally made for sports moms: a padded stadium cushion with a wearable blanket inside. My son plays on three sports teams, so I do a lot of sitting outside on bleachers and turf sidelines—and often at night, when it’s freezing. I’ve tried many things to keep warm, from heated jackets to HotHands, but nothing has worked as well as this water-resistant blanket, which unfurls to 50 x 70 inches and sports a clip at the front so you can wear it like a cape. It can also be used for picnics or as a spot for younger siblings to sit and read during tournaments. It’s also not hard to fold it back up and fit it inside the seat part (which is 1 inch thick without the blanket inside). It comes in six colors, so you can be sure to find one that matches your giftee’s kid’s team or school colors. —Kat Merck.

As a mom, I take a lot of photos of my family. A lot. And sometimes it feels like all those great photos of my son's milestones go to my camera roll and photo storage to die. There are two solutions I love for this that are incredibly giftable: a digital photo frame she can instantly upload images to, and a printed photo book where you can take the best of the best and put them at her fingertips. I have and love both for different reasons.

According to recent reports, I love the digital photo frame to add all the photos from a fun weekend at the San Diego Zoo or Renaissance Pleasure Faire for me to relive again and again, but I also love being able to pull a photo book from the bookshelf and relive a specific moment I know is waiting there for me. Aura makes my favorite digital photo frames (followed by Skylight's Calendar 2 if you want a multipurpose device, but Aura has no subscription fee if you only want photos), while Mixbook has been a favorite of mine for a while when it comes to printing photos, and has great starting prices for its photo books.

The graduation from diaper-bag-carrying mom to tote-full-of-snacks-and-clothes-changes mom to an adult who only needs to carry their own stuff is a parenting milestone that deserves celebration. This is my favorite grown-up mom bag, which holds only the essentials: water (because no matter how old your kids are, someone is going to get thirsty), cards, phone, and keys. The thick strap makes it comfortable to carry, and there’s a color, material, or theme for just about anyone’s vibe, including a newly introduced line of clear stadium versions. All WanderFull bags will hold any handle-less water bottle up to 11 inches tall and 3.5 inches in diameter. —Kat Merck.

Once my kiddo is asleep, you can find me parked on the couch playing video games. I upgraded to a Nintendo Switch 2 ($499) earlier this summer so I could finally buy and play Pokopia ($70), since it's exclusive to the upcoming console, and now my husband and I are completely hooked on the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time ($60) remake that came out a few weeks ago. It's also rapidly become an experience I can share with my son now that he's 4; he was been helping me and my husband replay Tears of the Kingdom, but now he's dubbed Ocarina of Time as “Big Little Link” and is obsessed with using the grappling hook and using up all of our arrows.

In a recent development, if you're not looking to upgrade her console just yet but need a Switch-friendly cozy game for her, Stardew Valley has another big update in the works and only costs $15. I'm also hoping we see Fields of Mistria ($14) come to the Switch eventually, but the full launch came out in August for Steam people and has major quality-of-life improvements if she has played Stardew one time too many. My husband also upgraded his gaming setup this summer with a Steam Machine (from $1,049), and I have big plans to start using it often for Fields of Mistria. If your mom loves games, she'll love any one of these new devices or new games, especially if she already got herself the new gadget as I did.

If a mom in your life is exploring her nonalcoholic drink options, The Zero Proof has some gift sets perfect to give so she can try out several things at once. I'm right now grounded from drinking any cocktails while I'm pregnant, but moms (and people in general) can have all kinds of reasons to want to explore unique, interesting drinks that are sans alcohol. I really liked this set for how many cool drinks it exposed me to, from bottles of nonalcoholic wine to knockoff cocktails. If you're looking to spend a little less, my favorites so far have been the Château del Ish Non-Alcoholic Sparkling Espumante ($20) and Lapo's Non-Alcoholic Melograno Mule ($20 for four).

It has been revealed that look, I love a Kindle, but if you want to get the best e-reader for your buck (or maybe she just wants an e-reader that isn't a Kindle), the answer is actually a Kobo. My favorite is the Kobo Libra Colour. It's cheaper than the Kindle Colorsoft and can also double as a digital notebook if you add on the $70 stylus. I also prefer Kobo's annotating options: You can write right on the pages instead of in weird pop-up margins and boxes only on Kindle. Kobo also has a page-turner remote ($34), which I love to pair with a pillow stand holder so I can lean back and relax without holding up my e-reader while I read. I gave a similar pillow stand to my mom, and now I can spot her last reading spot easily because that pillow is resting there.

You could also gift her one of the latest Kindles if she's a Kindle addict. Many of my friends are drooling over the new purple Ube color of the 12th-gen Kindle ($150), but my personal favorite is the Kindle Aluminum (I just wish it were cheaper!). There's also finally Kindle page-turn remote, the Kindle Click ($35).

If the mom you know is into LED red-light therapy, she probably already knows about face masks and hair growth devices like the one we recommend above, but there’s one area she’s probably neglecting: her hands. With aging comes loss of collagen, subcutaneous fat, and cumulative effects of UV exposure. I spent the first 26 years of my life living in California, where I rarely remembered to put sunscreen on the tops of my hands. Twenty years later, it shows—they’re wrinkly and have age spots and look like they belong to someone 15 years my senior. Trust me; no mom wants this. I’ve been using Omnilux’s FDA-cleared red-light glove for the past few months to try to mitigate some of the damage, and while I haven’t seen any changes yet (Omnilux says changes happen in four to six weeks, but in my experience with red-light masks, it typically takes much longer to see results), I very much enjoy using this device on its own. The soft silicone glove is comfortable to wear and warms as it heats up, so it feels good and works to reduce joint pain. It’s easy to do while I’m reading or watching TV—just three 10-minute sessions per week—and the rechargeable battery (USB-C) lasts a little over a week. If your giftee already spends 10 minutes at the end of the day relaxing in an LED face mask, she’ll know exactly what to do here. —Kat Merck.

Industry observers note that if you know a mom who loves to bird-watch (I know one!), you can upgrade her bird feeder to a smart one. Smart bird feeders add a camera to the feeder so she can see a close-up feed of the birds that come to hang out in her yard, and they're adorable to boot, for a little smart curb appeal. WIRED reviewer Kat Merck recommends the original Birdfy feeder as a great gift; it's her favorite smart bird feeder and comes in adorable colors to brighten your mom's yard and catch the eye of neighborhood birds. But the one she and I both have our eye on (her for her mother, me for myself) is the Birdfy Nest Duo, which is actually a birdhouse with two cameras so you can see the birds entering the nest outside and raising a family inside.

I love a backpack when I'm on the move with my 4-year-old, but one thing that annoys me is that things are hard to find inside, because packs are typically so deep. That's why I adore the Mina Baie Emmy Diaper Bag: It's a wide, shallow bag instead of a long one, making it easy to open and see most of what I store in it without digging around. I'm not toting diapers at the moment, but I've used it to pack a ton of snacks, toys, and spare clothing for my kid.

According to recent reports, I'm intrigued to see how using it with two kids goes—I chose the Emmy Midi, which is the midsize bag, but if you're a pumping parent or need to carry a ton of bottles with formula, you might want to try the larger Emmy Full. The stylish bag is made of vegan leather and can be converted from crossbody to tote to backpack mode, depending on which straps you use. Mina Baie doesn't include a changing kit, but sells one separately ($59) if you'd like to include it in your gift (or buy that as the gift to upgrade their existing bag of choice).

It has been revealed that if Mom loves entertaining—or just being festive—but doesn’t want to have to store a million different dishes, Nora Fleming’s modular serving-tray system is for her. First, pick a base—there are trays, baking dishes, utensil crocks, and even salt and pepper shakers. Then, pick one of dozens of hand-painted “Minis,” or ceramic accents (sold separately). There are holiday themes, sports team themes, and even ones for specific events like mah-jongg or BBQs.

Industry observers note that each base has a hole into which you can attach the Mini with a little rubber stopper. I tested the cracker tray with a harvest-themed Mini, and you wouldn’t know the tray didn’t come with the accent already attached. At the end of next month, I blueprint to swap it out for a Christmas tree Mini, and so on. Best part is that if Mom likes this setup, you’ll be set on gifts for the foreseeable future, provided you can keep finding upcoming Minis you think she’ll like. —Kat Merck.

According to recent reports, I'm expecting again, and this time I'm on a mission to find a good pregnancy pillow. I tried a large body pillow on the advice of another site for my first pregnancy, and it was honestly an awful experience—the pillow was too large and firm for me to comfortably use, let alone have room for both it and my growing midsection in my bed. Plus, it was heavy, which is annoying when your body already feels too cumbersome to move around.

So far, using the Wildbird Pregnancy Pillow has been the opposite. It's slim and light with just enough squish to add a little support under or around my belly without being difficult to get comfortable. It’s beautiful and easy to maneuver around. Wildbird also suggests it for other support positions postpartum, and I'm curious if those will work for me. But it makes for a beautiful gift for any expecting mom and will be one she's excited to put on her bed and curl up with at night.

It has been revealed that for most moms, showers are sacred—especially for moms of babies or younger kids. However, heavy metals, sediments, chlorine, and PFAS can cause health problems not just in drinking water but in water that touches the skin, as well. They can also cause buildup on hair and shower surfaces, making them harder to clean. Many municipalities—including mine—treat water with chlorine, and when I asked him which filter he'd recommend for my own shower, former WIRED reviewer Matthew Korfhage suggested the Weddell Duo. It's the only US filter he's found that has certification for chlorine and lead removal from NSF International, and it also cites third-party testing by IAPMO R&T showing it can remove PFAS, though there's no corresponding certification.

According to recent reports, still, the Duo has a 2.5-gallon-per-minute flow rate and can remove most chlorine from over 8,000 gallons' worth of showers. It's an in-line filter, so it's easy to install in minutes—just screw it in between your pipe and showerhead. It even comes with a little roll of waterproof tape to ensure a leak-free fit, and because of the horizontal orientation, installation won't affect the showerhead height. The filter needs to be replaced every three months, but refills only run about $25 each, compared with competitors like Filterbaby or Rorra, which can cost $40 to $45. —Kat Merck.

#2064. What does the blue snowflake icon mean for your Tesla battery?

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (708 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

What does the blue snowflake icon mean for your Tesla battery?

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (708 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Less available range, weaker regenerative braking and slower charging are all possible when that blue snowflake appears.
  • Tesla isn't sending you a little Easter egg for the holidays with that tiny blue snowflake that pops up next to the battery indicator.
  • You don't need to second-guess how much juice the EV has left 'cause Tesla marks the unavailable part in blue on the battery meter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Less available range, weaker regenerative braking and slower charging are all possible when that blue snowflake appears.

Tesla isn't sending you a little Easter egg for the holidays with that tiny blue snowflake that pops up next to the battery indicator. You're not getting a heads-up about the icy roads ahead either. Instead, that little indicator is actually telling you about your battery feeling the chills too. And when the battery gets cold enough to throw a blue snowflake light, some of its stored energy temporarily becomes unavailable.

You don't need to second-guess how much juice the EV has left 'cause Tesla marks the unavailable part in blue on the battery meter. But that temporarily disabled energy is usable again once the battery warms up as you drive around. Now, don't confuse the little snowflake indicator with the power your Tesla has lost overnight parked in your garage. The energy shown in blue on the battery meter is just the energy that's temporarily out of reach due to the cold.

Sources indicate that but even with a warmed-up battery, the cold will still bite a chunk out of your range. Keeping the cabin warm and toasty, combined with cold weather terrain depending on where you're driving, tends to take up more power than usual even for the regular gas-guzzler.

Sources indicate that other than some lost range on your EV, that festive blue snowflake also changes how your Tesla runs. Things like how long the car takes to charge and even that powerful acceleration could all feel a bit different. Regenerative braking also feels quite different if you're used to slowing down by taking your foot off the accelerator.

The whole idea behind regenerative braking is that when you lift off the accelerator pedal, energy that would otherwise be lost gets sent back to the battery. When the battery is on the colder side, it can't absorb that energy as it does in normal conditions, so expect your Tesla's regen effect to feel much weaker approaching a red light.

If you own a Model 3, check to see if your variant has a setting that allows stronger deceleration when regenerative braking is limited. Try to find the Apply Brakes When Regenerative Braking Is Limited option in Controls > Dynamics. Having this function on tells the car to use its normal, mechanical brakes to mimic full regenerative braking. Again, your ability to select this totally depends on the model and the software version running on your Tesla.

In a recent development, your Tesla might even show a separate icon that specifically tells you when regenerative braking isn't fully available. This looks a bit like a broken green brake disc with an electricity symbol inside. Either way, you're better off keeping that foot ready to hit the brakes yourself just to be safe.

Feel like a grumpy old Grinch and want that blue snowflake off? Well, Tesla won't let you do that manually, and the icon only goes away when your car's battery warms up again. Driving around or charging it should help, or instead of leaving the car in the cold, set up preconditioning for the battery. The way to do this is through Controls > Schedule on either the car's touchscreen or your Tesla app. Remotely turning on cabin climate controls is just what that high-voltage battery needs to get warmed up.

In a recent development, the smart thing to do here, if possible, is to keep the EV plugged in so all that preconditioning happens while the car's battery is receiving power continuously. Otherwise, you'll start the day with less charge than you were hoping to drive with, kind of defeating the whole purpose. If you want to fill up the EV faster with a Tesla Supercharger, start by setting it as your destination. This will get your EV's battery all warmed up and ready to be plugged in for fast charging with fewer delays.

There's no real indicator of what temperature actually triggers the snowflake icon, and Tesla hasn't given a timeframe for when it goes away either. The tech giant does, however, recommend that you gear up your car's climate settings to activate at least 30 to 45 minutes before leaving.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, after launching Moonlock for Mac last year, MacPaw is bringing its scam-detection app to iPhone today. Here are the details.

When MacPaw rolled out Moonlock on the Mac, the organization described its fresh app as something that “complements Apple’s built-in security tools, protects from Mac-specific malware, and helps you understand cybersecurity better.”.

In practice, the Mac app includes real-time protection against potential threats. Users can also manually scan their Mac for malware, including suspicious files hidden in system folders and email attachments.

Recent findings suggest that beyond that, Moonlock includes a VPN to encrypt internet traffic, a network inspector that indicates where apps are sending data and lets people block connections to specific countries, and an AI-powered scam detector that analyzes messages pasted into the app for signs of phishing. It also helps users review and adjust macOS security settings.

Today, MacPaw is launching Moonlock for iPhone, a move the firm indicates “helps people recognize potential scams, understand their iPhone’s security and take practical steps to improve it.”.

Unlike the Mac version, Moonlock for iPhone doesn’t scan for malware, as iOS prevents third-party apps from accessing other apps and their files. Instead, it focuses on identifying potential scams, checking for exposed personal information, and helping users improve their iPhone’s security.

On the iPhone, Moonlock lets owners quickly check suspicious texts, screenshots, and QR codes for phishing, in addition to checking whether their email addresses have appeared in known data breaches.

Recent findings suggest that as MacPaw explains it, Moonlock’s Scam Detect “helps people check suspicious messages they encounter throughout the day. Whether it’s a text message, a screenshot shared by a friend, or a QR code, people can paste, scan or share content directly with Moonlock and receive an assessment explaining why something may be suspicious.”.

Here’s Oleg Stukalenko, Head of Product Management at Moonlock by MacPaw, on today’s launch:.

Recent findings suggest that “When we released Moonlock, our goal was to make cybersecurity something anyone could understand and use. But so much of what people do today, from banking to everyday conversations, happens on their phones. Bringing Moonlock to iPhone felt like the natural next step. We want to help people spot a scam before they tap, see where their security stands, and know exactly what to do next.”.

MacPaw adds that Moonlock for iPhone also includes the following features:.

MacPaw’s Moonlock for iPhone is free to download, with subscriptions available for $9.99 per month or $49.99 per year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 is just hours away, and while console owners are looking forward to diving into the huge virtual world of Vice City, I'm sure that there are plenty of mobile players feeling left out.

After all, GTA 6 is currently the highest-rated game of all time on review aggregator Metacritic, with early reviews calling it a once-in-a-generation experience that you surely won't want to miss.

If you primarily game on a phone or tablet, unfortunately you're out of luck when it comes to playing GTA 6 on the go unless you already have access to a compatible cosnole – but there are plenty of Android native alternatives worth checking out instead.

It has been revealed that if you want to play GTA 6 on your phone and happen to own a PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X or Xbox Series S and a digital copy of the game, then remote play is an option. Both ecosystems let you stream the game from your console to your phone in order to play it in different rooms at home or, if the internet allows, when you're out and about.

If you own a PlayStation 5, then you'll need to download the PS Remote Play app and go through the on-screen process to link it to your console. There's no dedicated app for Xbox, and you instead need to visit the dedicated remote play website to get everything set up.

A compatible controller is recommended for the best experience, and you can use the one that came with your console or pick up a spare below.

In a recent development, this no-nonsense gamepad is fully compatible with Xbox Remote Play and easy to hook up to your mobile phone so a perfect choice for GTA 6. Just prop your phone up using a makeshift stand, and you can dive right in.

It has been revealed that for PS Remote Play, there's no better option than the official DualSense Wireless Controller. It's easy to pair and packed with unique features.

If you don't have access to the required hardware then you're not totally out of luck, read on for some other options.

Get the latest news from Android Central, your trusted companion in the world of Android.

In my view, the best alternative is to pick up one of the many native ports of older Grand Theft Auto titles available on the Google Play Store. The best part is that they don't cost anything to try out.

It has been revealed that GTA: Vice City - Definitive is an official remastered version of the 2002 installment Grand Theft Auto: Vice City. Set in the 1980s, it takes place in the same city as GTA 6 and offers its own unique storyline and a more condensed open world to explore. Yes, it's obviously not as technologically advanced as the new game (there has been more than two decades between them, after all) – but it's still a timeless classic and could be just the thing to tide you over until the FOMO wears off.

That initial free download nets you a 30-minute free trial, which you can then upgrade into the full game with a one-time in-app fee if you are enjoying the experience.

Industry observers note that you can do the same with GTA III - Definitive, which is a remaster for the third game in the series. GTA: San Andreas - Definitive is also available, though this entry costs money up front to play.

All three games have full touch control support, so you won't need to buy a separate controller either.

If you would rather play a more modern Grand Theft Auto game, then PC emulation is worth looking into.

You're going to need a seriously beefy phone for this, however, and I would recommend going with a dedicated gaming model like the RedMagic 10 Pro or the newly released RedMagic 11 Pro for the best performance.

These phones come with a built-in PC game emulator, which lets you download games you own from Steam with ease. If you own Grand Theft Auto 5 on Steam, you can get it running smoothly on your phone at around 720p resolution after fiddling with the graphics settings.

This lets you experience the whole previous entry, which is the next best thing to GTA 6.

You can even do this on any high-end mobile device by seeking out and downloading a compatible PC game emulator, but the setup process is much more complicated, and I wouldn't recommend it for beginners or those not willing to tinker with their tech.

If you're just after a game like the Grand Theft Auto series, then there are some native Android titles that offer similar gameplay.

I've been testing OneState Social RP over the last week or so, which is a free-to-play life role-playing game set in modern Los Angeles.

It has been revealed that it takes a bit of time to get going, but it's a surprisingly expansive experience that lets you pursue different career paths and engage in online multiplayer activities. You can become a police officer, for example, or join a criminal gang while working to earn money that you can spend buying homes, cars, and more.

Sources indicate that it's all based around big servers filled with hundreds of other players, who you're encouraged to interact and role-play with. It's like having a whole virtual world on your phone!

Sources indicate that retro City Rampage DX is also a great experience. It's only a few bucks to buy and offers top-down open-world action that's very reminiscent of the early GTA games. It's wacky, filled with fun challenges, and features more than 60 story missions to complete.

Finally, the popular free-to-play open-world RPG NTE: Neverness to Everness should be on your radar. It has slick anime graphics with an incredibly detailed and massive open-world city. The setting is more fantastical than the other two games that I've been talking about, but I personally enjoy the tense, supernatural tone of its main plot.

#2058. Latest Update: The vibe-coding revolution is coming to all the gadgets

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1613 w)
