The list of hacks hitting the US government over the last few months keeps growing.

The list of hacks hitting the US government over the last few months keeps growing.

Recent findings suggest that friday, it was reported that both the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the FBI were hacked. In reporting on the FBI hack, CNN noted that this is the second such attack on the agency in the last few months, this time targeting the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), which federal, state, and local law enforcement use to share information, including warrants and missing persons. President Donald Trump later confirmed the hack in an interview with Fox News. NBC first reported the USDA hack on Friday. According to Reuters:.

While the payments ​database is the known extent ​of the intrusion so far, the former ‌officials ⁠warned that the compromised system could provide a backdoor to more sensitive information, including food safety ​data and ​research on ⁠animal-borne illnesses, according to the report.

The breaches come following a week of major outages across several sectors, including at the FAA and NSA, which the government has sought to reassure the public were not the result of a cyberattack.

President Trump suggested that the breach of the FBI might not be an entirely bad thing, telling Fox News that, “Maybe we’ll learn about the voter fraud, all the voter fraud that took place,” and “wouldn’t it be great to learn about Russia, Russia, Russia?” referring to investigations into his ties to Russia.

In a recent development, the FBI suffered a breach, reported in late September, that allegedly compromised personal records of “all FBI employees and applicants.” This was followed by a hack of DHS, reported in October, comprising 40,000 employee records. In the wake of these major outages, the White House national cyber director, Sean Cairncross, stepped down this week.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • 2027 is going to be a relatively substantial iPhone release year for Apple.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo have been out for quite some time now, and despite that, it’s still incredibly challenging to order an iPhone Duo in a timely manner. If for whatever reason you’re considering skipping out on this year’s iPhones, here’s what you have to look forward to next year.

2027 is going to be a relatively substantial iPhone release year for Apple. First, the company will be continuing the iPhone 18 lineup after it introduced a split release schedule. Then, in the fall, the company will debut a newly introduced round of flagships in celebration of the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. Here’s what to expect.

Industry observers note that for the first time, Apple will be introducing its base iPhone in the spring. Upgrades for the iPhone 18 aren’t quite clear, though more RAM is one of the key rumors. Thermal upgrades will likely happen as well, as well as the fresh Apple C2 modem.

It’s possible Apple will patch the design to fall more in line with the iPhone 17 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro, though we don’t yet know.

This phone will of course equip the A20 chip, and it’ll probably start at the same $899 price point that iPhone 17 presently sits at – after it was increased from $799 in September.

This phone will most likely just end up being a chip bump from the A19 to A20 chip, and debut in the Spring alongside the iPhone 18. Earlier this year, reports indicated that Apple would share many components between the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, though it isn’t quite clear what that could mean for the devices.

Out of all of the spring iPhone releases, this one is the one to look forward to. After receiving a lukewarm reception with the initial iPhone Air model, Apple went back to the drawing board and decided to modify the design to fit an ultrawide camera into the device.

Personally, I don’t think an ultrawide camera is too key – though many people will see one camera on the back of the phone and immediately assume it’s less premium, so it’ll probably end up being an important upgrade for the sake of sales. Plus, ultrawide photos can be fun at times.

For the 20th anniversary of the iPhone, Apple is expected to debut a fully redesigned iPhone to celebrate. It’ll reportedly be much more glassy, feature significantly slimmer bezels, a quad curved display, and ditch the flat edge design of the iPhone 12 and later.

Personally, I’m slightly skeptical that this’ll truly be a replacement to the “Pro” phone for thermal reasons, but time will tell. iPhone Duo seemingly has strong thermals while not featuring an aluminum unibody, so my concern might not be relevant. It’ll offer two, larger display sizes: 6.4-inch and 7-inch. This largely comes from the bezel reduction.

I wish they prioritized the Telephoto camera more. I need that (whether it be on an Air or a Duo) way more than an Ultrawide.

If you’re holding out for iPhone 18 Pro, this “iPhone 20” is definitely the phone to wait out for.

Lastly, Apple will release a successor to its just-announced iPhone Duo next fall. Of course, you can expect next-generation Apple Silicon with the A21 Pro chip next year, but there aren’t many other substantial changes expected. Apple may bring proper Face ID to the outer display, an improvement from the recently-announced face unlock, but it’s unclear whether this feature will make the engineering cutoff date.

#1946. Latest Update: This built-in windows tool can tell if your DirectX has a problem

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (608 w)

General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: This built-in windows tool can tell if your DirectX has a problem

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (608 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • DxDiag is a handy and free resource for troubleshooting DirectX.
  • Industry observers note that directX is Microsoft's proprietary set of programming tools that help computer applications, especially games, communicate with your graphics card, audio and input devices.
  • DxDiag is a windows utility that scans your computer, collects technical system information and reports on installed DirectX components and drivers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

DxDiag is a handy and free resource for troubleshooting DirectX.

Industry observers note that directX is Microsoft's proprietary set of programming tools that help computer applications, especially games, communicate with your graphics card, audio and input devices. It allows software and hardware to work together to render graphics, play sound and deliver interactive multimedia experiences. If an application requires a DirectX capability but your computer doesn't support it, the application may fail to launch or crash mid-operation. Identifying the exact source behind these problems can be tricky, as outdated DirectX software, corrupt video card drivers or faulty Windows configuration could be contributing factors. This is where Microsoft's built-in DirectX diagnostic tool (DxDiag) can prove helpful.

DxDiag is a windows utility that scans your computer, collects technical system information and reports on installed DirectX components and drivers. The tool can be used as a convenient starting point to investigate graphics or audio-related issues. It can also generate a condensed text report that you can share with technical support persons for analysis. Understanding the capabilities and limitations of DxDiag can help you make informed decisions when troubleshooting sound, visual or application compatibility issues.

To run the built-in DirectX diagnostic tool, initiate the run command with the windows + R shortcut, then type "dxdiag" and press enter. You can also search for "dxdiag" in the Windows start menu and launch the utility from there. The DxDiag tool includes tabs for System, Display, Sound and Input. It is recommended to tick the "Check for WHQL digital signatures" checkbox to verify the integrity of installed drivers.

The System page includes details on your PC's motherboard, processor, memory and graphics card. It also displays the DirectX version installed on your computer. Meanwhile, the Display page offers a detailed overview of your graphics card, from driver version to supported DirectX features like Direct3D Acceleration and DirectX 12 Ultimate. Similarly, the Sound page includes information on connected audio devices and their driver details, while the Input page lists all IO devices, including your keyboard, mouse and other peripherals. Make sure to review the Notes section at the bottom of Display, Sound and Input pages, since it may list errors reported by DxDiag.

Sources indicate that can DxDiag tell if the DirectX on your computer is corrupted? While it can help identify complications with display, sound and input devices, DxDiag cannot conclusively determine or repair DirectX problems. Just because the utility displays a clean report, it doesn't necessarily rule out all hardware and game-specific issues that your computer might be experiencing.

If DxDiag reports display, sound or IO errors, start by comparing the affected component's driver version to the latest driver available. In case of discrepancy, consider downloading and installing the latest driver from the manufacturer's official website. While Windows upgrade often include driver updates, they are not always guaranteed be up to date. This could potentially result in outdated or incompatible drivers causing game-specific issues even when your hardware meets the recommended system requirements. In case of audio-specific issues, in addition to drivers, also consider verifying that you're using the correct playback device in the Windows sound panel. You may also want check if the affected application or game has a new update or patch addressing hardware-related bugs.

Recent findings suggest that if none of these steps end up resolving your problem, you can try running the sfc /scannow command as a administrator to scan and repair system files. If errors persist even after following these troubleshooting steps, it's recommended to contact Microsoft support and share your DxDiag report to help them investigate graphics, audio or other compatibility concerns in your PC.

It’s a rare thing for a film sequel to match or even surpass its predecessor; The Godfather Part II and Terminator 2: Judgement Day are the best known examples on a pretty short list. Go ahead and add Godzilla Minus Zero to that list. Director Takashi Yamazaki’s sequel to his critically acclaimed Godzilla Minus One (2023) is everything one could want in a Godzilla movie: human pathos, great special effects, and, ultimately, two giant kaiju duking it out over who gets to destroy Japan (and eventually the world) the most.

(Spoilers for the first film below. Spoilers for Minus Zero but no major reveals until after the gallery. We’ll give you a heads-up when we get there.).

As I wrote previously, Yamazaki wanted to return to Godzilla’s filmic roots with Minus One, setting the events in postwar Japan and tapping into the monster’s symbolic representation of the Japanese perspective on the 1940s nuclear holocaust—while also incorporating all-too-human themes of guilt and redemption. That first film focused on kamikaze pilot Kōichi Shikishima (Ryunosuke Kamiki), who struggled with survivor’s guilt after he failed to take action when Godzilla attacked the Japanese base on Odo Island in 1945.

Knocked unconscious, Kōichi survived and awoke to find his parents and many others were killed in the World War II bombing of Tokyo. Kōichi rebuilt a life with a woman named Noriko (Minami Hamabe) and the orphaned baby she rescued, Akiko (Sae Nagatani). But then Godzilla re-emerged, and Kōichi resolved to die fighting the monster to atone for Odo Island. Kōichi saved the day and lived to tell the tale. He reunited with Noriko, who had a strange black bruise on her neck. And we saw a chunk of Godzilla’s remains start to regenerate, leaving things open for a sequel.

Industry observers note that godzilla Minus One was a massive hit, both in Japan—where it remains one of the highest grossing Japanese films ever—and worldwide, racking up $116 million globally and winning an Oscar for best visual effects. Yamazaki said in interviews at the time that there had as yet been no talk of a sequel—while also hinting at future directions a sequel might explore. He later admitted it was way of planting a seed for what would become Godzilla Minus Zero.

Recent findings suggest that godzilla Minus Zero is set two years after the events of the first film, with Kamiki and Hamabe reprising their roles as Kōichi and Noriko, along with Nagatani as Akiko. The family is just trying to live in peace after the devastation Godzilla inflicted on their country. Alas, a new kaiju emerges, arriving via meteorite and using its tentacles to feed on local wildlife before morphing into a dragon-like creature that causes fresh rampaging destruction. Fans of the genre will recognize this creature as Ghidorah, whose appearance in the film was teased in the various trailers.

Recent findings suggest that it isn’t long before Kenji Noda (Hidetaka Yoshioka)—i.e., the dude with the magnificent wavy gray hair who is director of the Large-Scale Disaster Response Bureau—seeks out Kōichi for help in dealing with this new kaiju threat. His team is able to track Ghidorah’s movements via electrical storms and other pertinent weather patterns, thanks to meteorologist Makoto Aoyama (Masami Nagasawa). But the team has no idea how they might defeat this new threat to life and infrastructure. It’s hardly a spoiler to note that at some point, a regenerated Godzilla will come into play.

Recent findings suggest that (WARNING: significant spoilers appear below. Stop reading now if you haven’t seen the film.).

In a recent development, yamazaki has retained the visual tone that made the film’s predecessor so striking; it feels like classic Godzilla fare of yore, just with 21st century cutting-edge visual effects. If anything, he’s upped his game on the special effects front, reflecting the larger production budget he had to work with. (It’s also the first Japanese movie filmed specifically for IMAX and it’s well-worth seeing in that format.).

Much of that budget went toward bringing the central monsters to cinematic life, and Godzilla Minus Zero does not disappoint. Ghidorah, for instance, responds to a bombing attack by mutating into its famous three-headed King Ghidorah form, complete with a spiffy upcoming superpower: a “gravity beam” that lets the creature levitate entire houses (and, at one point, Godzilla) into the sky before dropping them back to the ground. And the kaiju vs. kaiju battle is spectacular in both scope and execution.

According to recent reports, yamazaki even managed to squeeze in what he called his “bucket-list” special effects shot inspired by a scene in 2008’s Cloverfield: Godzilla looming out of the Atlantic Ocean in front of the Statue of Liberty to wreck havoc on the statue and New York City in general. Granted, it occurs in a dream sequence of biologist Kanji Murakami (Min Tanaka), who survived the Hiroshima blast that killed his wife and children and longs for revenge. And it’s not just indulgence on the director’s part: the scene reinforces the traditional theme of linking Godzilla to nuclear radiation and the horrors of the atomic bomb.

Industry observers note that nor does Yamazaki ignore the human factor via the dilemma of his nuclear family trio. Kōichi must wrestle with his conscience: how can he risk his life again to battle a kaiju when it could mean leaving Akiko an orphan yet again should he fail? Noriko is infected with Godzilla’s radioactive G-cells—the only human to survive the mutations in her own body for so long. But her time could be running out, plus they’ve kept her infection secret for fear she will be taken away by the government for experimentation. Sometimes doing the right thing comes at great personal cost, and watching these quite ordinary people grapple with that reality brings emotional depth to the film.

The film ends on a suitably bittersweet note, and while Yamazaki hasn’t dropped any hints about a possible third film in the series, we’d love to learn more about Noriko’s strangely symbiotic connection to Godzilla via the G-cells in her bloodstream. Long may he reign.

Godzilla Minus Zero is still playing in theaters.

Countries agree to ‘start discussing options’ for rules around autonomous weapons.

Countries agree to ‘start discussing options’ for rules around autonomous weapons.

One of the items on the agenda for UN diplomats meeting in Geneva this week was working towards rules regarding the use of autonomous weapons, or so-called “killer robots.” Eventually, representatives left the meetings agreeing to “start discussing options” after a largely fruitless week of negotiations.

According to recent reports, before the negotiations got underway, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the guardian of the Geneva Conventions, said it was urgent for legally binding rules to be drafted within a year. That call was backed by the U.N. secretary-general and by Pope Leo.

Industry observers note that the compromise reached was that countries would instead have two years to propose regulations. Negotiations between countries on which regulations to adopt and how to enforce them will likely drag on well beyond that. Additionally, room was left for some of those yet-to-be-adopted regulations to remain “optional.”.

Humanitarian organizations and some countries see a need to urgently adopt legally binding rules as semi-autonomous weapons and drones have been responsible for a significant number of civilian deaths in conflicts around the globe, including in Ukraine, Gaza, and Sudan.

According to NPR, Russia, Israel, and the US proved to be the primary obstructions:.

On day one, Russia delayed proceedings by objecting to the meeting’s agenda. Then the United States proposed a five-year window to discuss nonbinding, optional guidelines for autonomous weapons.

We got two very different pictures of Nvidia this week, depending on whether you were focused on the company’s latest earnings report or the tech executives loudly calling for former CEO Jensen Huang’s return.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Kirsten Korosec, Tim De Chant, and I discussed the latest news from the AI chipmaker, which reported soaring revenue and insisted that it has no prepares for Huang to return.

Kirsten described this as “the tale of two Nvidias this week,” with the organization’s current executives assuring investors, “Hey, we’ve got this.” At the same time, “You’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back.” (The company’s falling stock price certainly suggests that Wall Street isn’t feeling reassured.).

Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity.

Kirsten Korosec: Nvidia will no longer sell its H200 chips in China. This was coming directly from the interim CEO Colette Kress, and that coincides with the Trump administration also talking about closing off what we have discussed in the past, which is this idea of remote access — really closing and tightening all these restrictions [so] the chips can’t make it into China.

What was happening is that data centers were being set up right outside, in countries like Malaysia and elsewhere, and then companies within China were remote accessing these chips, and so that’s now also been shut down.

A lot is happening on the China front that is so much bigger than Nvidia, but Nvidia came out publicly and said, “Nope, we’re shutting this part down.” I’ll be very curious to see if this changes, maybe in the first half of 2027.

In a recent development, tim De Chant: I’d love to be a fly on the wall in some of these Trump administration conversations, because they were much more stringent in terms of export controls at the end of the first Trump administration, and that continued through the Biden administration, where they really restricted Nvidia’s ability to export chips to China. I think that something changed in the last couple of years that really opened Nvidia’s ability to sell in the country.

Anthony Ha: One of the things that really surprised me as we were preparing for this episode was [learning that critics] of Nvidia’s stance towards China estimate that 20% of their business comes from China.

And again, that’s not something you’re going to see directly in their financials, because that’s not direct sales to Chinese companies. But they’re saying, “A lot of the chips that are getting sold to companies in Malaysia or other companies in East Asia or Southeast Asia are going to end up [used by companies in] China eventually.” And so that could be — if Nvidia is really serious about this, I think this is something that’s very much in flux — that could actually be a pretty significant blow to their bottom line.

According to recent reports, kirsten: Although Nvidia’s bottom line is doing just fine. In every possible way, their guidance was incredible. They beat expectations. They have a long pipeline.

It was really interesting because you have that happening, and then you have all this noise happening in social media, and also a number of other tech conferences were happening this past week — Dealbook Summit, there [were] a few others in which you had the highest profile people that you can think of in the tech world commenting on Jensen [Huang], and Jensen himself commenting.

So it’s like the tale of two Nvidias this week. You’ve got the earnings and the current executives really talking about, “Hey, we’ve got this.” In fact, that was the last line that Collette Kress said [on the earnings call]. And then at the exact same time, or in parallel, you’ve got Elon Musk and others out there really pushing to bring Jensen back, circulating a petition, Jensen himself saying that he’s prepared to come back. So it’s really quite the drama that we are definitely not done with, by the way.

Anthony: Although I think that what the folks who’d like to see Jensen Huang come back would say is that this most recent quarter is the last quarter under him. This is the [last of the] good times that we’re seeing under him. And so we don’t know how well Nvidia will do without him.

It seems like Nvidia’s public stance right now [on Huang’s possible return] is, “No, that’s not happening.” But Nvidia’s public stance a week and a half before that was, “We stand behind Jensen. We have every confidence in his leadership.”.

So depending on the various pressures on them, you can imagine that changing. I don’t know what it would take for that to happen. I don’t necessarily think it’s that likely, but I also don’t think that just because they’re saying it’s not happening now doesn’t mean it will never happen.

Kirsten:  Sure, never say never.

In a recent development, tim: Right, never say never. I do think that to some extent, their steadfastness and how rapidly they shot down the petitions asking for Jensen to return suggests there’s maybe a little bit more going on behind the scenes than we know on the outside. So that’s probably something to watch in the coming weeks.

Industry observers note that kirsten: I think that the board is trying to be in control here, and they don’t want to be forced into a decision because someone like Elon Musk is saying that it needs to happen. And so, even if there is a day in which Jensen returns — which I think is pretty unlikely, especially because the investigation into how much and who knew what about chips being sold, allegedly, secretly to China. We don’t know the full picture of that yet. But even if they did have the full picture, they want to present control, and they definitely don’t want to appear like they have deference to some other tech billionaire out there.

Tim: I’m sure they’re looking at what happened at OpenAI and not wanting to repeat that.

Anthony: I imagine the dynamic’s a little bit different, since Nvidia is a public firm. So, I’m not an expert on this, but I would guess it would be much harder for you Jensen Huang to come back and just toss out a bunch of board members.

This follows the launch of GIF creation in the Gemini app yesterday. Powered by Gemini Omni 1.2 Flash, select GIF from the Format menu or specify “Create a GIF” in your prompt. Google frames this feature as an alternative to searching for GIFs.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Amazon is taking its accusations that the Council is driving up prices offline and onto your packages.

Amazon is taking its accusations that the Council is driving up prices offline and onto your packages.

Sources indicate that amazon is leaving no venue unexplored in its fight against the Newly introduced York City Council and the Delivery Protection Act. The organization is now putting labels on shipments claiming that the Council could add up to $5 to any Amazon order. The Delivery Protection Act would effectively ban the sort of third-party arrangements Amazon currently uses to deliver many packages, including small companies and independent contractors. Last-mile delivery firms operating warehouses would need to be licensed by the city and directly employ their workers.

Earlier this week, Amazon started showing notifications in its mobile app and on its website reading “Attention NYC Council could add up to $5 per order.” Now the manufacturer is including an almost identical message on shipping labels.

Amazon claims that the bill, if passed, “would likely mean slower and more expensive delivery for millions of customers in New York City,” and has threatened to move its warehouses outside of the city. However, labor unions, Council Speaker Julie Menin, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani have countered that the manufacturer is attempting to “threaten New Yorkers and intimidate this City Council” and is acting out of “greed,” pointing to Amazon’s market cap of nearly $3 trillion.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

President Donald Trump suggested Saturday that there could be a bright spot in the latest incursion into the FBI computer database.

The president confirmed in an interview with Fox News that a system has been breached that houses information used by law enforcement at all levels to share criminal justice information.

The hackers accessed the National Criminal Information Center (NCIC), a database that includes FBI fingerprint records, wanted persons, violent felons, missing persons and related information, two people familiar with the matter told MS NOW. The database is restricted to law enforcement use but not classified and it is unclear what data was extracted.

CNN had first reported on the suspected hack, citing sources familiar with the concern.

In a wide-ranging interview on Fox, Trump noted there could be upside from the news.

According to recent reports, "Maybe we'll learn about the voter fraud, all the voter fraud that took place," he stated. "I always like to put things on a positive spin.".

Industry observers note that this would be the second recent intrusion into the FBI system; the previous one came in September, when a group known as "ShinyHunters" broke into an FBI jobs website. The result compromised data on current and former FBI employees and shut down part of the agency's operations until the problem was resolved.

Trump remarked it's possible there could be information gleaned from the latest hack.

"I wonder who's doing it, because wouldn't it be great to learn about Russia, Russia, Russia?" he said. "People should hear about it, because it actually put our country in danger, and so maybe we'll learn things that we wouldn't have learned otherwise.".

The FBI did not immediately respond to a CNBC request for comment.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Signal revealed Friday that it’s limiting users’ ability to take screenshots within the secure messaging app — a response to what President Meredith Whittaker described as the “existential threat” of operating systems that integrate agentic AI.

Whittaker wrote that by giving AI agents the ability to “scan” the information on consumers’ screens, Windows, Android, and macOS/iOS “are undermining Signal’s ability to independently guarantee privacy.”.

Industry observers note that “Now, in service of AI agentic capabilities, your sensitive data is being captured, stored, and made accessible to whatever local database or remote server an OS-level AI agent is using at that moment,” she noted. “All of this is outside of Signal’s control once the data has been captured, and imperils the privacy of all the participants in a conversation.”.

In a recent development, signal already sought to limit these risks by blocking screenshots of its Windows app by default. Now it’s adding similar restrictions in Android and iOS.

That stated, users can disable this setting if they wish, which Whittaker said would “break our privacy guarantees.” She also admitted this is an “incomplete” solution, as it doesn’t “address other more sneaky ways AI agents could potentially access application data.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that if you look up at the sky tonight, you'll notice the Moon is looking noticeably fuller than it did earlier in the week. We're still in the Waxing Gibbous phase, which falls between the First Quarter and Full Moon, but we're getting closer to the Full Moon every night.

As of Saturday, Nov. 21, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Gibbous phase, with 85% of its surface visible.

Sources indicate that if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Imbrium and Vaporum, as well as the Kepler Crater. With binoculars, you'll also see the Mare Frigoris, the Clavius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And if you have a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 15 and 17 landing spots, and the Rima Hyginus.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

It has been revealed that according to NASA, the Moon goes through a complete cycle of phases roughly every 29.5 days. As it orbits Earth, the portion of its sunlit surface visible to us changes, giving rise to the different lunar phases. The cycle begins with a New Moon, progresses to a Full Moon, and then gradually returns to a New Moon before starting all over again.

Newly introduced Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

Industry observers note that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

If you like playing daily word games like Wordle, then Hurdle is a great game to add to your routine.

There are five rounds to the game. The first round sees you trying to guess the word, with correct, misplaced, and incorrect letters shown in each guess. If you guess the correct answer, it'll take you to the next hurdle, providing the answer to the last hurdle as your first guess. This can give you several clues or none, depending on the words. For the final hurdle, every correct answer from previous hurdles is shown, with correct and misplaced letters clearly shown.

An key note is that the number of times a letter is highlighted from previous guesses does necessarily indicate the number of times that letter appears in the final hurdle.

Nike still outfits some of the world’s top athletes. If you’re a basketball player, I’d recommend skipping the Nike Dunks and getting a pair of Kobe Protros, like Caitlin Clark. If you’re a runner, Nike recently updated the classic Pegasus. If you’re looking for a low-key street shoe that’s not an Adidas Samba, get the Nike Blazers.

It has been revealed that there are tons of Nike’s bestselling shoes on sale right now, including: Nike Dunk Low and Dunk Low Retro SE at 24% off (with multiple under $100), Zoom Vomero 5 at 24% off, Nike Free Metcon 6 at 32% off, and custom Metcon 10 for as low as $155. Plus, classics are on sale, with Air Max 270 up to 30% off, Air Force 1 Low Retro up to 33% off, or Air Force 1 ‘07 LV8 for under $80. Be sure to check out these heavy discounts on tons of Nike styles, from classic to contemporary.

It has been revealed that nike got its start as a running firm, and it still makes the best running apparel on the market. My particular favorites are the firm-support, high-waisted ⅞ running leggings (because I’m short) and the running rain jacket, which is understated enough to wear as an everyday rain jacket. In a recent development, nike is constantly launching new products and collabs based on trends, history, celebrity endorsements, and more, ensuring they always have an exciting, fresh launch at the ready. #1924. Netflixs best Christmas movies now streaming

Netflixs best Christmas movies now streaming

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 19 min read (3749 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~19 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, do you need a little Christmas?
  • Industry observers note that this winter, the streaming service has a festive lineup perfect for whiling away the chilly days and nights at home or picking up your mood if it needs a lift.
  • Sources indicate that and, of course, if you're looking for specific recommendations of excellence, we've made a list and checked it twice.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, do you need a little Christmas? Right this very minute? Then we recommend you head to Netflix, where an array of holiday movies are present and ready to be unwrapped.

Industry observers note that this winter, the streaming service has a festive lineup perfect for whiling away the chilly days and nights at home or picking up your mood if it needs a lift. Whether you're seeking something joyful, tragic, or even action-packed, Netflix has a holiday movie to suit your desire.

Sources indicate that and, of course, if you're looking for specific recommendations of excellence, we've made a list and checked it twice. Here are some of the best Christmas movies streaming on Netflix this winter season.

Industry observers note that american pop star Sabrina Carpenter offers a holiday variety show of her own, available only on Netflix. A Nonsense Christmas with Sabrina Carpenter features festive songs, comedy sketches, and a gaggle of celebrity guests, including Chappell Roan, Tyla, Shania Twain, Quinta Brunson, and Megan Stalter.

With a runtime of 50 minutes, this is a short and sweet treat for the girls, the gays, and everyone else charmed by Carpenter's breezy and bawdy brand of pop music. — Kristy Puchko, Entertainment Editor.

How to watch: A Nonsense Christmas with Sabrina Carpenter is now streaming on Netflix.

According to recent reports, perhaps the most polarizing movie of the holiday season, Love Actually is a collection of interlocking vignettes all about — well — love. There's the story of the timid prime minister (Hugh Grant) who falls for a sassy staff member (Martine McCutcheon), the story of the widower (Liam Neeson) guiding his stepson through puppy love, the shy American (Laura Linney) with a crush on her office mate (Rodrigo Santoro), and Alan Rickman playing his most villainous holiday role as the heartbreaker of Emma Thompson. (I too have seen Die Hard. I said what I said.).

Recent findings suggest that written and directed by Richard Curtis, Love Actually is both wildly popular and widely derided for some of its quirks. But the awesome star power and unapologetically joyful love stories keep us coming back year after year.* — K.P.

How to watch: Love Actually is now streaming on Netflix.

Sources indicate that thirsty for some seasonal rom-com fun? Then you'll want to plunge into Champagne Problems.

Industry observers note that minka Kelly stars as Sydney Price, an ambitious American executive who's traveling to Paris for business. There, like many a rom-com heroine before her, she meets a dashing stranger (Tom Wozniczka), and naturally they share a big, swoonworthy kiss — only to find out they are enemies! (We love an enemies-to-friends arc.).

See, Sydney is on a mission to acquire Chateau Cassell, a family-owned business in France's Champagne region. Her handsome kisser? It just so happens he's Henri Cassell, son of Chateau Cassell's founder, and he doesn't want his dad to sell to some boorish American. Sparks are sure to fly, as these two can't deny their chemistry.* — K.P.

How to watch: Champagne Problems is now streaming on Netflix.

It has been revealed that imagine Tootsie but as a gender-flipped holiday rom-com. Hear me out.

In Tootsie, Dustin Hoffman plays an actor who feels there are no good roles for men. So he dresses in drag to get a role as a woman on a TV show. Now, in My Secret Santa, it's that — except a single mom wants to get her daughter discounted snowboarding lessons, so applies for a job as a ski resort Santa by taking on the look and persona of an old man who happens to look like Santa (if he was made of plastic).

According to recent reports, there's just one problem. Out of her holly jolly drag, she catches the eye of a handsome man (Ryan Eggold) who has ties to the resort. If they fall for each other, could her Santa secret get out? What would that mean for her daughter's snowboarding lessons? And can love win when it's based on a beard-faced lie?* — K.P.

How to watch: My Secret Santa is now streaming on Netflix.

In a recent development, director Jaume Collet-Serra has excited audiences with the shark-infested Shallows, the twisted killer thriller Orphan, and Liam Neeson vehicles like Non-Stop and Unknown. Now, he's teaming up with Taron Egerton (Rocketman, Kingsman: The Secret Service) for an unusual holiday adventure.

Sources indicate that set in a Los Angeles airport on Christmas Eve, Carry-On follows a TSA agent (Egerton) who is desperate to stop a suspicious package from making it to a deadly destination. There are some truly wild things in this cat-and-mouse game that pits an eager Egerton in everyday hero mode against Jason Bateman as a snarling mercenary hellbent on getting his package delivered, whatever the collateral damage. Those seeking fresh thrills will relish Collet-Serra's competent approach to suspense, and may well feel their travel anxiety spike. But hey, can we all admit that asking English hunk Egerton to do an American accent is a crime against cinema? It's not even that he's bad at at. It's more that, in a world where so much is terrible, why waste even a moment by not hearing Egerton in his native tongue?* — K.P.

How to watch: Carry-On is now streaming on Netflix.

It has been revealed that not a movie but a three-season series out of Norway, Home for Christmas is a must-watch for the holiday season. The wildly charming Ida Elise Broch stars as Johanne, a 30-year-old single nurse who is tired of being chucked to the kids' table for the holidays. So, she tells a little lie, claiming she'll be bringing a beau to her parents' Christmas Eve dinner. Now, she just needs to find someone before the holiday is upon her!

With episodes running under 30 minutes, Home for Christmas is a short-and-sweet treat that explores love and sex while also confronting the frustrating social standards put on women to mate up. While there are doses of sobering drama as Johanne confronts loneliness, family discord, and loss, the series is overwhelmingly warm and funny. And if you're not into subtitles, the overdub is perfect for watching while gift-wrapping! — K.P.

How to watch: Home for Christmas Seasons 1-3 are now streaming on Netflix.

Industry observers note that true Dolly Parton fans understand the country star to be more than the celebrity, hero, legend, and icon popular cultural has whittled her down to be. Dolly, you see, is a lifestyle — a way of being, an all-encompassing perspective on personhood. In Dolly Parton's Christmas on the Square, that high-level plane of existence gets the sparkly holiday treatment in a musical romp as shining as Dolly herself. Sure, the whole thing is ridiculously old-fashioned and not surprising in any way. But it's also got exquisite pageantry with Christmas spirit to spare. And of course, the songs are fantastic. — Alison Foreman, Entertainment Reporter.

How to watch: Dolly Parton's Christmas on the Square is now streaming on Netflix.

If you want to see Kurt Russell slap his butt as Santa, then you've come to the right place. Writer Matt Lieberman (Free Guy) and director Clay Kaytis reimagine the traditional "Someone's gotta save Christmas!" narrative in this familiar but still fun holiday outing with Russell as Old Saint Nick. Judah Lewis and Darby Camp star as a brother and sister who, in trying to catch proof of Santa, get more than they bargained for. Should you fall in love with this over-the-top universe, definitely check out The Christmas Chronicles: Part Two, which features Russell's life partner, Goldie Hawn, as Mrs. Claus. — A.F.

How to watch: The Christmas Chronicles is now streaming on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that impress and entertain anyone you're with this holiday season by cuing up Netflix's hidden gem Alien Xmas. This sci-fi adventure from the team behind Elf's iconic stop-motion scenes delivers a charming tale of intergalactic thieves descending upon Earth to steal everything — including Christmas. Part How the Grinch Stole Christmas, part WALL-E, Alien Xmas is an adorable animated adventure that's great for kids and adults alike, with a timeless message. — A.F.

How to watch: Alien Xmas is now streaming on Netflix.

It has been revealed that is A Christmas Prince a movie? Nay, it is a journey. Join our heroine, American journalist Amber Moore (Rose McIver) as she takes on an undercover assignment in the far-off country of Aldovia in this schmaltzy rom-com opposite Ben Lamb as the titular Christmas prince. This movie is exactly what you think it is, and if that's what you're the mood for, excellent news: Its even more outrageous sequels, A Christmas Prince: The Royal Wedding and A Christmas Prince: The Royal Baby, are streaming now too. God save King Richard Bevan Charlton. Long may he reign. — A.F.

How to watch: A Christmas Prince is now streaming on Netflix.

In a recent development, remember simpler times with Netflix's 2015 Christmas spectacular A Very Murray Christmas. Directed by Sofia Coppola, this magical presentation featuring Bill Murray has a very loose plot that primarily serves as a revolving door for guest appearances and musical numbers. With a runtime of just 56 minutes, the infectious levity of the project and its supporting cast (including Miley Cyrus, Amy Poehler, George Clooney, Chris Rock, and more) is sure to have you smiling fast. — A.F.

How to watch: A Very Murray Christmas is now streaming on Netflix.

Director Luke Snellin's feature-length debut is without question the right pick for anyone on a YA kick come the holidays. With a stellar cast including Shameik Moore, Kiernan Shipka, Isabela Merced, Joan Cusack, and more, Let It Snow adapts the popular novel of the same name — telling three stories of love, friendship, and magic on Christmas Eve in a single small town. Sure, this movie is another offshoot of Love Actually's tremendous influence over the holiday genre catalog. But it's a good one. — A.F.

How to watch: Let It Snow is now streaming on Netflix.

Industry observers note that want a different spin on Santa Klaus? Then check out director Sergio Pablos' utterly enchanting — and sharply funny — Klaus, which was nominated for Best Animated Film at the 2020 Academy Awards. Playing like a festive spin on The Emperor's New Groove, this inventive animated adventure centers on a self-centered rich boy named Jesper Johansson (voiced by a pitch-perfect Jason Schwartzman), who is pitched out of his life of privilege into a remote village that's divided by an intense feud. He's there to deliver the mail, and — in a convoluted but charming way — concocts a blueprint that involves a reclusive woodworker (J.K. Simmons) with a treasure trove of carved toys and a giddy group of kiddies eager to write letters for gift-getting wishes. How will all of that turn to holiday cheer? Discovering that is just a part of the whimsical magic of Klaus. — K.P.

How to watch: Klaus is now streaming on Netflix.

Sources indicate that jingle Jangle: A Christmas Journey is absurd in all the ways you actually want. As Mashable's Angie Han wrote in her official review of the steampunk musical extravaganza, "It's all entirely too much, in a way that feels just right — like a Christmas stocking bursting at the seams with too many goodies." Surprisingly sweet and an important step for Black representation in Christmas films, Jingle Jangle will make you happy this holiday. Pinky promise. — A.F.

How to watch: Jingle Jangle: A Christmas Journey is now streaming on Netflix.

According to recent reports, sure, Christmas technically already has an origin story, but some of us are looking for a more epic, secular, fantastical tale to sink our teeth into. Enter: A Boy Called Christmas, adapted from the 2015 Matt Haig novel of the same name.

Featuring Henry Lawfull, Sally Hawkins, Kristen Wiig, Stephen Merchant, Jim Broadbent, Toby Jones, and Dame Maggie Smith, A Boy Called Christmas follows a young boy who embarks on an incredible adventure through the ice and snow to find the land of the elves and bring hope to his people. He's got a trusty mouse sidekick at his side and a can-do attitude. Hold on to your cocoa, folks; this movie is positively radiating with holiday spirit! — Kristina Grosspietsch, Freelance Contributing Writer.

How to watch: A Boy Called Christmas is now streaming on Netflix.

After a bad breakup, Peter (Michael Urie) heads home to Newly introduced Hampshire for the holidays with his best friend Nick (Philemon Chambers) in tow, hatching a foolproof proposal to pretend to date Nick so his family won't harp on his recent heartbreak. As soon as he arrives, however, Peter's family sets him up with a hunky local spin instructor. And when things go well, Peter begins to wonder if maybe it’s time to move back to New Hampshire for good. Will Nick agree?

Written by Chad Hodge and directed by Michael Mayer — Broadway veterans, both! — 2021's Single All the Way is an excellent romantic comedy for the holidays. It's funny, it's charming, and it's got the right amount of true human emotion to make this a new feel-good Christmas classic. Oh, and the absolutely stacked cast (which includes Jennifer Coolidge, Kathy Najimy, and Luke Macfarlane) doesn’t hurt! — K.G.

How to watch: Single All the Way is now streaming on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that what is a "good movie," really? Does it need a coherent plot, believable stakes, and characters that act like human beings? Sure. So, by that metric, Falling for Christmas is not a good movie. And yet, it is the movie that ushered in the Lindsay Lohan renaissance of the 2020s, and for that, we are extremely grateful! Yes, it's silly — but it's the best kind of silly, mindless fluff.

In a recent development, lohan is wooden but charming as Sierra Belmont, a wealthy, disconnected heiress about to get engaged to her flighty, absurd influencer BF Tad (George Young). But then she falls off a mountain (seriously) and wakes up in the care of down-to-earth widowed dad Jake (Chord Overstreet), with no memory of what happened! You heard that correctly; this is not a drill! It's a Christmas-amnesia-rom-com, people!!!! — K.G.

How to watch: Falling for Christmas is now streaming on Netflix.

In the same fictional Christmas-verse as Netflix's A Christmas Prince, Stacy (Vanessa Hudgens) is an American chef on her way to the made-up European country of Belgravia for a baking competition. There she runs into Lady Margaret Delacourt (also Hudgens), future wife of Belgravia's crown prince, who is looking for a break from the country's rabid media. Her solution? That she and Stacy switch places, of course! What could go wrong? Surely, no one will notice an American nobody pretending to be a duchess! Surely, these two women won't definitely fall in love with the men in each other's lives... right? Right?!

Sources indicate that zany, bubbly, and the opposite of subtle, The Princess Switch — along with sequels The Princess Switch: Switched Again and The Princess Switch 3: Romancing the Star — is a perfect watch for when you're in the mood for some sugary-sweet nonsense. — K.G.

How to watch: The Princess Switch is now streaming on Netflix.

Brooke Shields is Sophie, an American novelist looking to escape the PR frenzy around her newest book. She absconds to a small town in Scotland where her grandfather once lived, and after feeling a connection to the place, promptly tries to buy the rundown castle. (Sure!) The catch? Current owner Myles (Cary Elwes) refuses to sell unless Sophie can survive both of them living there together for 90 days. It's like an only-one-bed situation, but with an entire castle. Myles hopes he can scare Sophie off… but as time goes on, does he still want her to go?

It has been revealed that so many Christmas romantic comedies feature stiff acting, but Shields and Elwes both abound with energy and charisma. A Castle for Christmas is a no-brainer holiday watch: It's cheerful, it's charming, and you're genuinely rooting for these two to get together! — K.G.

How to watch: A Castle for Christmas is now streaming on Netflix.

According to recent reports, the Knight Before Christmas has all your favorite holiday movie tropes: a precocious little girl, a woman who no longer believes in love, and the man who is going to change her mind. Except the man in question here is Sir Cole (Josh Whitehouse), a medieval knight who has been transported to the present and doesn't understand a thing about this upcoming world. Good thing the woman, Brooke (Vanessa Hudgens, Netflix Christmas queen!), is there to help him figure it all out. The Knight Before Christmas is just as cheesy as you think it is, but that doesn't mean it's not a fun watch! It’s like a Christmas-y Kate & Leopold, but with less gravitas and more hijinks. — K.G.

How to watch: The Knight Before Christmas is now streaming on Netflix.

According to recent reports, lindsay Lohan brings her winsome energy to Our Little Secret, a cute comedy about past loves, big secrets, and the absolute awkwardness of meeting your partner's family for the first time. Once childhood sweethearts, Avery (Lohan) and Logan (Ian Harding) were everything to each other. After a surprise holiday wedding proposal goes badly, they lose touch for 10 years, only to turn up at the same family gathering — because they're dating siblings! With shades of Anyone but You, Our Little Secret has the pair hiding their past relationship to keep things chill and avoid the ire of an intense mother hen (Kristin Chenoweth). Amid holiday hijinks and incredible social pressure, will these old flames reignite like a Yule log? — K.P.

How to watch: Our Little Secret is now streaming on Netflix.

Sources indicate that the Full Monty meets holiday rom-com in The Merry Gentleman. When her big-city dreams take a big hit, professional dancer Ashley (Britt Robertson) finds fresh purpose in her small hometown. There, her parents' performance venue, The Rhythm Room, is at risk of closing. But perhaps one hit show could save the theater? More specifically, an all-male dance review combining Christmas music and strapping hunks ready to strip down from their gay apparel for a whooping audience. While counting down to a Christmas that'll make or break her family, Ashley gets her groove back, not only by throwing herself into this creative Christmas production but also by falling for a buff — and a bit gruff — handyman (Chad Michael Murray). Heads up: The Merry Gentleman is nowhere near as flashy or smoking hot as Magic Mike. But if you're seeking to get a bit heated in these chilly months, it'll go down like a cup of cocoa. — K.P.

How to watch: The Merry Gentlemen is now streaming on Netflix.

In a recent development, there are plenty of Santa stories to choose from each winter. (Heck, there are several on this list!) But only one has a script co-written by Love Actually's Richard Curtis — and a Father Christmas voiced by Succession's Brian Cox! Based on Curtis' adorable children's book trilogy, That Christmas is an animated adventure that features a debonair Santa Claus and a wise-cracking reindeer sidekick, as well as a mighty blizzard that pitches parents into peril, leaving their kids to band together to save the holiday. And hey, maybe they'll get a little help from a certain icon of gift-giving and goodwill. — K.P.

How to watch: That Christmas is now streaming on Netflix.

Recent findings suggest that what if Frosty were a hunk? That's the premise of this cheeky holiday rom-com that's a mix of festive, funny, and mildly horny. Mean Girls Lacey Chabert and Schitt's Creek's Dustin Milligan star in this tale of Girl Meets Snowman. She's a small-town diner owner whose heartbreak doesn't stop her from giving plenty of warmth and joy to others. He is a buff snowman, carved — complete with nipples and rippling abs! — for a winter festival display. But a holiday wish brings him to life, turning him into a flesh-and-blood himbo/Golden Retriever boyfriend... who melts if he gets too hot. (Hm. Well, that's less than ideal.) Will love find a way? And did screenwriter Russell Hainline mean to reference Terminator with a nude intro that leads into a festive crime spree?

If you're intrigued, you'll treasure Hot Frosty. — K.P.

How to watch: Hot Frosty is now streaming on Netflix.

A festive tale of fate, love, and music frolics forth in Meet Me Next Christmas. Christina Milian stars as Layla, a gorgeous and generous "miracle worker" whose not-for-profit work secures scholarships for students to attend HBCUs. She deserves a holiday that's out of the movies... And it will be.

In a recent development, screenwriters Molly Haldeman and Camilla Rubis cleverly pluck elements from The Holiday, Serendipity, and Sleepless in Seattle to create an NYC-set fairy tale about taking a chance on a fresh romance. After a meet-cute with a dashing man (Kofi Siriboe) in an airport lounge, lovelorn Layla becomes convinced that tickets to see Pentatonix at a sold-out Christmas Eve show will be all she needs to make a love connection that will last. To get this hot ticket, she'll need the help of a committed (and cute) broker (Devale Ellis), who will be her guide through the decadent halls, quirky characters, and oddball antics that is Christmas in New York City. — K.P.

Industry observers note that how to watch: Meet Me Next Christmas is now streaming on Netflix. Recommended deals for you HBO Max — top pick for premium content Disney+ — best for families Peacock — low-cost choice for live sport.

Thank the gods, Percy Jackson remembered it should be funny

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1001 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Mashable

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Disney+'s Percy Jackson and the Olympians series has done an admirable job of adapting the Greek mythology-inspired adventures of Rick Riordan's novels.
  • According to recent reports, the book series are narrated by Percy Jackson (Walker Scobell) himself, whose internal monologue contains its fair range of sass and hilariously deadpan descriptions of the strange things that happen to him.
  • The TV series borrows these chapter headings for its own episode titles, but loses a significant chunk of the humor that make them land on the page.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disney+'s Percy Jackson and the Olympians series has done an admirable job of adapting the Greek mythology-inspired adventures of Rick Riordan's novels. But it has consistently struggled with a key aspect of of the books: their humor.

According to recent reports, the book series are narrated by Percy Jackson (Walker Scobell) himself, whose internal monologue contains its fair range of sass and hilariously deadpan descriptions of the strange things that happen to him. Case in point, every book's irreverent chapter titles, which kick off with the iconic "I Accidentally Vaporize My Pre-Algebra Teacher" and go on to include such hits as "I Battle My Jerk Relative" and "Everybody Hates Me but the Horse.".

The TV series borrows these chapter headings for its own episode titles, but loses a significant chunk of the humor that make them land on the page. It sands down much of the wisecracking banter between Percy and his questing companions, turning them into more stoic fantasy heroes. Yes, Season 2 features one of the books' funniest moments: the fan-favorite scene of Grover (Aryan Simhadri) wearing a wedding dress to escape from cyclops Polyphemus. (It throws Percy in a dress too for good measure.) But it also misses out on the smaller wordplay or misunderstandings that drew big laughs from the books, like when Percy mistakes the word "hubris" for "hummus." It's a solid joke, as well as a reminder that Percy is just a kid caught in the crossfires of a mythic war. In missing out on these gags, small as they may be, the show has failed to let Percy and his companions be kids, and also struggled to capture the books' distinct tone.

Thankfully, the first two episodes of Percy Jackson and the Olympians Season 3 prove to be a refreshing change of pace, right from their very first moments. The season begins with a tense monster fight for Thalia (Tamara Smart), during which Percy intervenes and helps her kills her foe. When she tells him she had everything under control, a car bursts into flames in the background.

It's a classic gag, one that by no means reinvents the wheel. But it gets better when Annabeth (Leah Sava Jeffries) asks Percy to put out the fire. As she and Thalia have a serious chat, we see him exasperatedly playing firefighter in the background. Here is a perfect example of how to balance the Percy Jackson and the Olympians books' high stakes with humor, and the TV series keeps it up from there.

Turns out, the key to unlocking Percy Jackson's comic potential is the contentious relationship between Percy and Thalia. The pair butt heads throughout the first two episodes, over everything from how to deal with Kronos ally Luke (Charlie Bushnell) to undertaking a quest. There's real dramatic tension there, but Percy Jackson and the Olympians emphasizes it with a running undercurrent of sassy snapping. When Thalia mentions her dream of battling Percy to the death, she wonders if it will come true.

"No!" Percy says, affronted. Then, as a follow-up beat, he asks, "Who won?".

Recent findings suggest that in addition to the often sarcastic back-and-forth between Percy and Thalia, Percy Jackson and the Olympians finds other ways to levels up its humor. Its fight scenes get the occasional jolt of laughter, like when Annabeth orders Grover to "goat kick" a foe. The show also leans further into the kinds of descriptions Percy would give in his internal monologue in the books. When he sets foot in the imposing military academy of Westover, he remarks it looks like students are "training for Dracula's army." That's not a line that's actually in The Titan's Curse (Percy likens it to "an evil knight's castle" instead), yet it feels like it could be ripped straight from its pages.

Industry observers note that elsewhere, the series finds genuinely funny ways to cut its intense storyline. After Annabeth reminds Percy he said he'd burn down Olympus to save her, he utters a hapless, "I was having a bad day when I said that." A later scene involving Percy and Thalia waiting for a prophecy from the Oracle also left me in stitches. Who other than Percy Jackson would ask a mummified Oracle for a high five in the hopes of waking her up?

Recent findings suggest that even the gods are funnier this season. Apollo (Hubert Smielecki) being a hot-shot bro who jams out to "Walking on Sunshine" contrasts perfectly with his sister, fierce huntress Artemis (Dafne Keen). Hearing her snarl "We are twins" after he keeps calling her "kid sis" is exactly the level of petty family drama I want to see from the Olympians.

Industry observers note that none of this increased humor detracts from Percy Jackson and the Olympians' dramatic stakes. Far from it! The dark moments — and book readers know that this season will get dark — still land, even more so now that they've been juxtaposed with genuine lightness. Like in the books, that lightness emphasizes just how young these characters are, which makes their brutal trials even more heartbreaking. And with The Titan's Curse's fan-favorite "dam" jokes on the way, confirmed by Scobell himself, we know we'll be in for a lot more humor combined with that heartbreak.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Google Workspace is that ubiquitous modern business tool that almost feels invisible. We use it every day here at WIRED, whether that's for writing first drafts of articles in Docs, analyzing data in Sheets, or sharing files in Drive. And recently, I've been using the Gemini AI implementation that's built right into these tools, which is handy in all sorts of ways.

Google Workspace grants access to all kinds of productivity features that can help streamline processes and increase communication within a team or organization. It's not free, but here's the good news: If you're looking at a Workspace account for yourself (or for your team), Google is offering discounts until the end of 2026 using one of the Google Workspace coupon codes below. You can save up to 14 percent on looks for the first three months, whether you're signing up as an individual or as a business. Either way, the Google Workspace promo code down below is what you want to use.

Industry observers note that there are some notable differences between each Workspace initiative – I’ll dig into them in the next section – but all three plans come with access to the full slate of Workspace apps. You get Gmail, Drive, Calendar, and Meet, of course, but even the cheapest Starter plan includes basic access to Google’s other apps, such as NotebookLM and Gemini inside the Workspace suite. If you want to save, make sure to click one of the promo codes at the top of this page to secure your discount.

Google offers four different Workspace plans, though only three are relevant for most people. There’s Starter, Standard, and Plus, as well as Enterprise, which is only available if you contact Google’s sales team. There isn’t a minimum number of customers on any of the plans, but the bottom three options (Starter, Standard, and Plus) support up to 300 users. If you need more than that, you’ll need an Enterprise blueprint.

In a recent development, although you have access to all the apps regardless of the initiative you choose, there are some important differences, particularly between the Starter and Standard plans. Both include secure storage through Google Drive, but Starter comes with 30GB per user while Standard comes with a massive 2TB per user. Plus bumps that up to 5TB per user. Across all plans, storage is in a shared pool, so each additional user adds to the total pool of storage your organization can use.

Gemini is also a significant difference between Starter and Standard. Although both have access to the Gemini app, Starter only has Gemini in Gmail and Vids. Standard (and Plus) includes Gemini across the full suite, including in Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Meet, and Chat.

According to recent reports, starter is a great option for anyone just getting started, regardless of whether you’re a freelancer or a small business with a handful of employees. In addition to 30GB per user and limited access to Gemini, Starter comes with a few other limitations. It doesn’t support e-signatures in Docs, nor advanced features of Meet, such as noise cancellation. The bread and butter of Workspace is all here, though. You get a custom domain in Gmail, up to 100 participants in Meet, and the full Google suite of productivity apps.

Standard, as the name suggests, is Workspace proper, and it’s built for teams that need room to grow. That demonstrates up most clearly in storage space, jumping from 30GB to 2TB per user. Standard basically cuts all the red tape on Starter. There aren’t any limitations on Gemini (it’s available across the full suite), Meet features like noise cancellation are available, and you can host up to 150 participants in a Meet call. Standard even comes with expanded access to NotebookLM, Google’s AI-driven note and research tool, with different chat modes and up to 20 generative audio overviews per day.

At the top of the range is Plus, which is focused on larger businesses. You don’t get any extra apps with this plan, but you do get 5TB of storage per user, along with up to 500 participants in Meet calls. The real reason to upgrade to Plus is security and admin controls, however. It includes Vault for data retention, along with LDAP access—basically a server for centralized account management, if you aren’t familiar.

It has been revealed that most people should use the Standard blueprint, not only for the large amount of storage space over Starter, but also due to the extra Gemini functionality. If you need to upgrade to Plus down the line, you can. And, more than likely, you’ll have a member of your IT team begging you to do so.

Sources indicate that google has updated Workspace a lot over the past several months, building in fresh functionalities via Gemini throughout the suite. But earlier this year, Google unveiled that it’s bringing all of those functionalities together through Workspace Flows. It’s a no-code automation tool that lets you build automatic workflows; i.e., patch a Sheet when there’s a new email in Gmail from a particular address. The interesting thing about Flows, however, is that Gemini is built into it.

You can set up basic automations, which is great given how interconnected Google’s Workspace apps already are, but Flows become powerful when you throw Gems into the mix. Gems are AI agents built with Gemini, and you can create them with specific parameters.

In a recent development, let me give you an example. Say you need a marketing plan, and an employee sends you a draft. You can have a workflow set up with a Gem that’s been trained on the budget, requirements, and tone of the campaign to quickly know if it can be approved or not. Or, you can create a Gem to scan your email, trained on your organization chart and role responsibilities, to notify you whenever you receive an email that has action items for you.

Industry observers note that flows give you a way to add a bit of context and reasoning to the often rigid constraints of simple automation systems, and they can save you a lot of time in the process. You may be able to gather customer feedback and put it into Sheets easily, for example, but Gemini can automatically sort, summarize, and categorize that feedback so you know what you should tackle first. Flows are centralized in Workspace, as well; you don’t need to install add-ons or configure anything outside of setting up your Workspace account.

Google Workspace Flows is a upcoming tool integrated with Google Workspace. It is powered by Google’s Gemini AI and helps you get tasks done with Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Calendar and Chat. It can fix up emails, make intends, correct sheets, or write a follow-up message. No apps or links are needed.

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI fans waited more than a decade for a new installment of the best-selling video game of all time.
  • Now they've grown up and they're itching to not just play GTA 6; they're also eager to participate in the Grand Theft Auto discourse.
  • From the debate over killing or sparing a character named Arnold to cataloguing all the wildlife cameos to the game's hot soundtrack, GTA 6 is driving countless conversations amongst players, including teens.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, grand Theft Auto VI fans waited more than a decade for a new installment of the best-selling video game of all time. That includes teens who were toddlers when the game's last chapter debuted.

Now they've grown up and they're itching to not just play GTA 6; they're also eager to participate in the Grand Theft Auto discourse.

From the debate over killing or sparing a character named Arnold to cataloguing all the wildlife cameos to the game's hot soundtrack, GTA 6 is driving countless conversations amongst players, including teens.

In a recent development, but the game is rated 17+ and features adult content, including sex, strip clubs, drugs, graphic violence, and murder. So, many parents whose teens want to play GTA 6 will likely find themselves in the familiar yet tricky position of balancing their child's interests and social life with exposure to content they feel violates their family's values.

Dr. Brett Biller, a child psychologist at Hackensack University Medical Center, wants parents to know it's OK — even advisable, in his opinion — to say no to GTA 6.

Biller has no problem with video games in general. In fact, he acknowledges how online interactive games can have benefits, like socializing with friends over play.

Ultimately, however, he believes exposing tweens and teens to GTA 6's hyperrealistic community violence is simply not worth it.

"The negative consequences can outweigh the positive impact," Biller indicates.

Recent findings suggest that while research doesn't prove that video game violence causes aggressive behavior, Biller notes there's a correlation between between violence in the home and aggression. That makes Biller cautious about exposing kids and teens to violent video games.

Recent findings suggest that killing zombies, he notes, is much different than murdering human characters, and younger children don't consistently grasp the difference between fantasy and reality. Yet Biller says older teens can also struggle in this way, especially given the realism of GTA 6. Plus, the game may normalize community violence by putting a teen player in the shoes of a thief or killer.

Meanwhile, teens with a history of witnessing or experiencing violence who play GTA 6 may find it difficult to manage the game's stimuli and their feelings about the content, Biller adds.

Beyond concerns about violence, parents may say no because they understand how playing GTA 6 will affect their child's mood, sleep, and personality.

"We, as caregivers, are responsible for making decisions that are in the best interest of our children," Biller says.

He recommends parents who won't permit their teen to play GTA 6 validate their child's frustration or fears of being left out.

Parents can also model how peer pressure is real and hard, because they feel it when other adults let their teen play GTA 6.

Recent findings suggest that biller claims this conversation presents a good opportunity to help a teen understand that standing up for their principles isn't always easy. He suggests parents explore with their teen other activities they can do with friends instead of playing GTA 6.

While some parents might feel better about playing alongside their teen, instead of the teen playing with friends, Biller says this approach is a "double-edged sword" that requires care and vigilance.

On one hand, parents who co-play have ample chances to point out and discuss concerning content or themes with their teen. On the other, co-playing can model to a teen that violence is fun or not a major deal.

In more cases than not, Biller finds that parents use this approach when they don't feel confident saying no or to justify their own choices.

Common Sense Media, a nonprofit organization that reviews and rates entertainment content, described GTA 6 as an "extremely mature crime game" for adults 18 and older.

According to recent reports, still, its review notes that only parents will know if their older teen is ready to play. Either way, Jasmine Hood Miller, director of family resources and content strategy for Common Sense Media, claims parents should talk to their teen about the game.

Topics for discussion can include what looks fun about GTA 6, how women are depicted in sex scenes and strip clubs, and whether they think they'd hurt people in the game, or have done so.

"It can be uncomfortable to talk about some of those topics," Miller states. "But honestly, if your kid is not talking to you, they're talking to someone else.".

Recent findings suggest that miller adds that these conversations should feel low pressure and not like a lecture. Instead, Miller encourages parents to be curious and nonjudgemental.

If a teen plays or watches the game at a friend's house, even after their parent has noted no, Biller recommends better understanding the context and validating their teen's feelings.

"Reward them for being honest," he notes. "We want them to continue to be open with us." #1911. Breaking: Voyager 1 had a data outage when it hit one light day. It still does.

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1022 w)
